item.title: NHL commissioner Bettman familiar with both Bills, Foley and Laurie
item.description: NHL commissioner Gary Bettman addresses the media Tuesday at PPG Paints Arena prior to the Golden Knights-Pittsburgh Penguins game. PITTSBURGH — Whoever gets the NBA expansion franchise in Las Vegas will do so having done business with Gary Bettman. The NHL commissioner obviously knows Bill Foley, the owner of the Vegas Golden Knights. He also knows Bill Laurie, who along with his wife Nancy, owned the St. Louis Blues. Both Foley and Laurie are reportedly the finalists to be granted the NBA expansion rights to Las Vegas with the price tag, including the construction of a new arena for the team to play, reportedly around $13 billion. The NBA is expected to announce its plans to expand before the end of 2026, perhaps in the coming weeks. Bettman, who was in Pittsburgh Tuesday to take in the Golden Knights-Penguins game at PPG Paints Arena, said both men are of high character and he believes would do well with an NBA team in Las Vegas. “Bill ran a first class organization (in St. Louis),” Bettman said of Laurie, who owned the Blues from 1999 to 2011. “We had no complaints about the things he did when he owned the Blues.” Bettman has not talked to NBA commissioner Adam Silver about the possibility of pro basketball coming to Las Vegas. And he won’t takes sides as to which Bill would be the more successful one. “I think he’d say that first and foremost, he’s a basketball guy,” Bettman said of Bill Laurie.” We wish him good luck. “I won’t predict or prognosticate on how he’ll do or how another basketball team would do in Vegas. I’m more than happy with the Vegas Golden Knights.” Back in 2000, Laurie made an unsuccessful bid to acquire the Vancouver Grizzlies and move the NBA team to St. Louis. The Grizzlies were eventually sold to Michael Heisley and left Canada for Memphis in 2001. He also failed in attempts to acquire the Denver Nuggets and the Charlotte Hornets. When asked to compare the ownership styles of the two Bills, Bettman smiled and said, “I think Bill Foley had a little more success.” As for NHL expansion, Bettman said there was no news to report. Houston, Austin, Texas and Atlanta have been mentioned prominently as candidates for the NHL should it decide to grow from its current 32 teams. “Still working through it,” he said. Regarding the present, Bettman was asked about empty seats in NHL arenas this season as rising costs and a struggling economy may be keeping fans from traveling to watch their team play. It wasn’t mentioned specifically, but the Golden Knights’ sellout streak which came to an end last month after 420 games, including playoffs when just 15,977 attended a Thursday night game against the Toronto Maple Leafs at T-Mobile Arena, which officially seats 17,367 for hockey. “Overall, attendance is up,” he said. “You’ve had a couple of instances where you’ve had some empty seats. But it’s not the same reason in each place. But attendance is up.”

item.title: McDavid vs. Hellebuyck: The NHL’s Best Showdown Is Here
item.description: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Stop scrolling past the promo codes and look at the actual hockey happening Tuesday night. The real story isn’t about bonus cash; it is about two Connors facing off in a game that ESPN staff flagged as a “must-see game of the week.” You do not need a bet to know this matchup carries more weight than most seasons. It is a rare collision of elite talent that fans have waited years to see on the ice. Connor McDavid is currently threatening NHL scoring records with nine goals and 30 assists through just 15 games. That pace is insane, and it puts the Edmonton Oilers in the spotlight. On the other side, the Devils are hosting a specific version of Connor Hellebuyck that the league has never seen before. As a Devil, his debut home start in New Jersey is probable, shifting the net’s entire dynamic. Greg Wyshynski summed up the stakes perfectly when he wrote, “It’s the Connor vs. Connor matchup we all want to see. McDavid threatening NHL scoring records. Hellebuyck likely making his first home start in New Jersey as a member of the Devils. Obviously, this is the thing that all of the United States will be focused on next Tuesday night.” That line hits hard because it is true. The Numbers Behind the Hype Stats do not lie, and both players’ current form makes this a must-watch event. McDavid’s 30 assists in 15 games show he is driving the offense harder than anyone else in the league. The Devils have a new anchor in goal, and Hellebuyck brings a track record of excellence to a team that needs it now. Per ESPN, the game kicks off at 7:30 p.m. ET on Tuesday, giving fans a prime slot to catch the action. This is not just another regular season game; it is a key test for both rosters. The narrative around McDavid is simple: he is breaking records while his team tries to keep up. The narrative around Hellebuyck is about adaptation. He has to prove he can lead a new squad in front of a hostile crowd. New Jersey home debuts for Devils member Hellebuyck appear likely, per reports. That single fact creates a storyline that goes deeper than the score. It is about a player proving himself in a new city. Everyone loves a good promo code, but the hockey on the ice is the only thing that truly matters. The game features the league’s best playmaker against one of its best goalies. The matchup is set for Tuesday night, and the stakes are high for both franchises. ESPN highlighted this specific game because it offers a clear window into the future of the league. You can see the best of the sport in one hour. The Devils need Hellebuyck to settle in fast , while the Oilers need McDavid to keep his historic pace going. This is the kind of game that defines a season. The players are ready, the teams are set, and the puck drops at 7:30 p.m.

item.title: Raiders owner announces approach toward starting Fernando Mendoza
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Las Vegas Raiders drafted Fernando Mendoza with the number one overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft. However, the former Heisman Trophy winner has been relegated to backup duties while veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins runs the offense. Cousins has had an impressive season individually, throwing 19 passing touchdowns and posting a 101.4 quarterback rating, but the Raiders are just 4-4 on the season and on the outside looking in at the current AFC playoff picture. Many are wondering when Vegas will make the switch to get Mendoza game experience, but fans shouldn’t look to team owner Mark Davis to pressure the coaching staff into making a change. “From me, there’s absolutely no pressure whatsoever,” Davis told CNBC Sport’s Michael Ozanian on Monday. “Today, there’s a lot of pressure put on teams when they draft a guy No. 1 that you have to play him right away,” Davis added. “That’s why I think we were so fortunate to get Kirk Cousins as someone who could bridge the gap and let this young man learn a lot about what football is in the pros, the speed of the game, and the things that have to be done.” Although Davis is taking a patient approach with the quarterback, it’s not because he isn’t picking things up. “He’s picking it up great, but I think we’re fortunate that he doesn’t have to go out and play,” Davis said. “I’ve seen quarterbacks get fast-tracked onto the field, and they may do well, but they don’t learn all the intricacies of footwork and everything else that it takes. So they’re limited in their development, maybe throughout their career.” Whenever Mendoza does get the nod, Davis thinks he has the intangibles and leadership traits to flourish in the NFL. “I tell people jokingly, if he can play football, he’s going to be amazing,” Davis said. “Because he’s got every other intangible that you would want in a person. He’s a hard worker. He’s a sponge.” The post Raiders owner announces approach toward starting Fernando Mendoza appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Gasperini warns: “I don’t know when Gollini will be back.”
item.description: Gasperini warns: “I don’t know when Gollini will be back.” Pierluigi Gollini, shortly before Manchester United vs. Roma, suffered a back injury and was unable to play in the match, which the Giallorossi lost 3-2. The Roman side, having taken a two-goal lead (Soulé, Malen (R)), then fell behind in the second half, conceding three goals (Bruno Fernandes (R), Da Cunha scored a brace). Gollini’s replacement, Vasquez, also saved the former Udinese player’s penalty, but the referee retaken the penalty for Cristante’s alleged invasion of the penalty area. The goalkeeper, reinstated after Svilar’s injury, bears no particular responsibility for the goals conceded, except for the final one, where he could have been more ready to hit his own post, but Da Cunha’s shot was still difficult to stop given the monstrous power with which he fired. The former AC Milan player could however defend Roma’s goal on Saturday in view of the last match before the break against Sassuolo. Gian Piero Gasperini, in a press conference, discussed Gollini’s condition. He was sidelined today against Manchester United with a back injury and replaced by Vasquez: “I don’t know if he’ll be able to return on Saturday, we’ll see.” The alarm bells are ringing at Roma, with the former AC Milan goalkeeper warming up to defend the Giallorossi goal again on Saturday ahead of Roma vs. Sassuolo. The next few days will be crucial to see if Gollini will be able to grit his teeth.

item.title: Where to watch Grand Slam of Curling Masters: Schedule, times, channels, live streams, scores for 2026
item.description: Where to watch Grand Slam of Curling Masters: Schedule, times, channels, live streams, scores for 2026 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 2026 Grand Slam of Curling series continues this week with the GSOC Masters from Alberta. Based on the opener three weeks ago in Victoria, the teams to beat in Medicine Hat will be Team Schwaller on the men's side and Team Einarson on the women's. It was the second GSOC win for Yannick Schwaller and the seventh for Canadian stalwart Kerri Einarson. Everyone will be gunning for those two teams, but there are plenty of other contenders including two other Canadian favourites in defending champions Team Dunstone in the men's division and Team Homan on the women's side. Here's all you need to know to watch all the action this week. Where to watch Grand Slam of Curling Masters TV channels: CBC, Sportsnet Live streams: Fubo , Sportsnet+, Rock Channel Fans can stream the entire Grand Slam of Curling Masters via Rock Channel, which will have exclusive live coverage of the morning draws each day, along with games not selected for featured spots on the main broadcast the rest of the day. One featured game during the afternoon and evening draws will air on Sportsnet channels and Sportsnet+ from Tuesday through Friday, along with Saturday's quarterfinals and Sunday's finals. The men's and women's semifinals will air on CBC and Sportsnet+ and can also be streamed via Fubo . Grand Slam of Curling Masters schedule, scores 2026 All times listed below are Eastern. item.title: Raphinha se olvida del fútbol y recuerda a Jesús de Miguel: «Hoy es un día muy duro»
item.description: Raphinha se olvida del fútbol y recuerda a Jesús de Miguel: «Hoy es un día muy duro» El brasileño, autor de dos goles ante el Aston Villa, dedicó sus primeras palabras a la familia del futbolista del CD Tenerife y reconoció la dificultad de afrontar el encuentro tras conocer la noticia. Raphinha fue uno de los grandes protagonistas de la victoria del FC Barcelona ante el Aston Villa, pero su actuación quedó en un segundo plano al finalizar el encuentro. El delantero brasileño, autor de un doblete, quiso dejar a un lado el resultado y los goles para acordarse de Jesús de Miguel , futbolista del CD Tenerife fallecido este martes a los 30 años. En declaraciones a Movistar +, el azulgrana trasladó sus condolencias a los familiares y allegados del jugador. https://mediacenter-cdn.socblaugrana.com/Declaraciones-de-Raphinha-sobre-el-fallecimiento-de-Jesus-de-Miguel.mp4 «No quiero hablar de fútbol. Quiero dedicar la victoria a la afición. Quiero mandar mucha fuerza a la familia de Jesús y que descanse en paz. Hoy no es un día para hablar de fútbol», expresó el brasileño. Un golpe para todo el vestuario La noticia del fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel también tuvo un fuerte impacto en el entorno del Barcelona. Raphinha reconoció que los jugadores conocieron lo sucedido antes del encuentro y que resultó especialmente complicado concentrarse en la competición. «Esto le puede pasar a cualquiera. Es muy duro, cuando hemos visto la noticia… es complicado. Piensas que tienes que jugar también», explicó el atacante, poniendo voz a los sentimientos que acompañaron al equipo durante una jornada marcada por la tristeza. Dos goles que quedaron en segundo plano Sobre el terreno de juego, Raphinha había firmado una actuación destacada con dos tantos que contribuyeron al triunfo azulgrana frente al Aston Villa. Sin embargo, el brasileño insistió en que no era el momento de detenerse en su rendimiento individual ni en el resultado. «Hoy no es un buen día para hablar de fútbol y quiero mandar mucho ánimo para la familia de Jesús», concluyó ante los micrófonos de Movistar +. De esta manera, el delantero del Barça quiso dedicar la victoria y su actuación a Jesús de Miguel, sumándose a las numerosas muestras de cariño que el fútbol español está trasladando a su familia, al CD Tenerife y a toda la afición blanquiazul. - Publicidad -

item.title: Latest MLB Proposal To Players Pushes Salary Cap Out To 2028
item.description: Major League Baseball is facing a lockout on December 1st as they continue to push a salary cap system. Today they offered up to push the cap system out to 2028, along with other changes. (Photo by Erica Denhoff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With less than a month to go before the labor agreement between Major League Baseball and its players is set to expire, the league offered up a new proposal on Tuesday that sees their push for a salary cap pushed out to 2028 to allow clubs at the bottom of the player payroll spectrum additional time to transition to the proposed salary floor. The league’s transition proposal to the MLB Players Association delays salary cap and floor implementation to 2028 for a smoother transition, with a projected cap of $180.2 million and a floor of $150 million. Other key reforms proposed include raising minimum salaries, reducing roster churn, eliminating draft pick compensation, and expanding free-agent access. The plan aims to balance team competitiveness, player benefits, and market stability. The cap and floor figures include player salaries and benefits. Signing bonuses to amateur players are excluded. In the latest salary cap proposal, the current Competitive Balance Tax (CBT) – or as it is more commonly known as the Luxury Tax system in place – would be extended by a year. The proposal does not adjust the thresholds or penalties. The base threshold for the 2026 season was $244 million. The base tax rates and surcharges in the final year of the current labor agreement would also retain the status quo. That alone would be something the MLBPA would oppose, given that they have proposed increasing the upper threshold to $300 million as part of the next labor deal. In a fact sheet released by the league, the issue of the proceeds from extending the CBT for an additional year was addressed by saying, “MLB would agree to allocate the players’ share of 2026 CBT proceeds (normally used to fund contributions to players’ 401(k) accounts in future seasons) to players as a bonus based on service accrued in 2026 ($285,000 to each player that received a full year of service, $213,400 to any player with three quarters of a year of service, $142,300 to any player with half a year of service, and $71,100 for any player with a quarter year of service).” Proposal To Increase The Minimum Salary Additionally, the league offered up several ways the minimum salary for the league’s players as part of the proposal. MLB will increase the minimum salary from $780,000 in 2026 to $1,000,000 in 2027 for players with at least two years of service and $900,000 for players with less than 2 years of service. Players with less than 2 years of service will also earn at least $100,000 under the Pre-Arbitration Bonus Program, bringing their total compensation to at least $1,000,000, if they receive a full year of service (and spend less than half the season on the IL). Today they offered up to push the cap system out to 2028, along with other changes. (Photo by Erica Denhoff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With less than a month to go before the labor agreement between Major League Baseball and its players is set to expire, the league offered up a new proposal on Tuesday that sees their push for a salary cap pushed out to 2028 to allow clubs at the bottom of the player payroll spectrum additional time to transition to the proposed salary floor. The league’s transition proposal to the MLB Players Association delays salary cap and floor implementation to 2028 for a smoother transition, with a projected cap of $180.2 million and a floor of $150 million. Other key reforms proposed include raising minimum salaries, reducing roster churn, eliminating draft pick compensation, and expanding free-agent access. The plan aims to balance team competitiveness, player benefits, and market stability. The cap and floor figures include player salaries and benefits. Signing bonuses to amateur players are excluded. In the latest salary cap proposal, the current Competitive Balance Tax (CBT) – or as it is more commonly known as the Luxury Tax system in place – would be extended by a year. The proposal does not adjust the thresholds or penalties. The base threshold for the 2026 season was $244 million. The base tax rates and surcharges in the final year of the current labor agreement would also retain the status quo. That alone would be something the MLBPA would oppose, given that they have proposed increasing the upper threshold to $300 million as part of the next labor deal. In a fact sheet released by the league, the issue of the proceeds from extending the CBT for an additional year was addressed by saying, “MLB would agree to allocate the players’ share of 2026 CBT proceeds (normally used to fund contributions to players’ 401(k) accounts in future seasons) to players as a bonus based on service accrued in 2026 ($285,000 to each player that received a full year of service, $213,400 to any player with three quarters of a year of service, $142,300 to any player with half a year of service, and $71,100 for any player with a quarter year of service).” Proposal To Increase The Minimum Salary Additionally, the league offered up several ways the minimum salary for the league’s players as part of the proposal. MLB will increase the minimum salary from $780,000 in 2026 to $1,000,000 in 2027 for players with at least two years of service and $900,000 for players with less than 2 years of service. Players with less than 2 years of service will also earn at least $100,000 under the Pre-Arbitration Bonus Program, bringing their total compensation to at least $1,000,000, if they receive a full year of service (and spend less than half the season on the IL). The increase of the minimum salary to $1,000,000 would be the largest year-over year increase in the minimum salary in Baseball history (and is about $100,000 higher than the previous largest increase). In future years, the minimum salary will increase with growth in the Cap and Floor. “We recognize that clubs will need a full offseason to prepare to operate within the cap and floor system,” said MLB spokesman Glen Caplin. “Therefore, with this offseason already underway, we proposed today to begin the cap and floor system in 2028. This proposal would allow a smoother transition into the cap and floor system without delaying key player benefits, including earlier free agency, a $1 million minimum salary, a 30% increase to the pre-arbitration bonus pool, and transactional reform that will reduce roster churn. The projected salary cap and floor for 2028 continues to provide more money for major league players while leveling the playing field and giving more teams the ability to participate in the free agent market and retain their homegrown stars so that every fan believes their team has a fair chance to win it all.” Multiple changes have been offered up by the league, such as offering up revenue sharing of all local media rights as a way to increase economic parity, but have only done so by attaching the changes to the implementation of a salary cap. With today’s proposal, the league opened the door to saying that negotiating a phase-in timeline and procedures for implementation of the salary cap and floor was on the table. The MLBPA immediately pushed back on the proposal. “Coming off another incredible season of baseball, MLB owners continue proposing blowing up the current system and replacing it with one designed to line their pockets and increase their franchise values.” While the Luxury Tax payrolls for 2026 have not yet been released, in MLB’s latest proposal, they highlight how the cap system would affect two-thirds of the league’s CBT payrolls. Based on the 2026 CBT payrolls, the following clubs would be required to increase those payrolls that include benefits to reach the proposed $180.2 million floor. While the figures are not revealed, the league indicates that those increases would total $636 million across 12 clubs: Miami Marlins Cleveland Guardians St. Louis Cardinals Tampa Bay Rays Washington Nationals Chicago White Sox Minnesota Twins Colorado Rockies Pittsburgh Pirates Athletics Cincinnati Reds Milwaukee Brewers It should be noted that of the 12 listed, four reached the 2026 MLB postseason, including the World Series Champion Milwaukee Brewers and the ALCS-winning Tampa Bay Rays. Based on the 2026 CBT payrolls, the following eight clubs would need to lower their CBT payrolls by a combined $528 million. Los Angeles Dodgers New York Mets New York Yankees Philadelphia Phillies Toronto Blue Jays San Diego Padres Boston Red Sox Of these eight, four made the postseason, with the Dodgers reaching the NLCS before the Brewers swept them. While MLB has tweaked their latest proposal to push out the cap and floor, other proposed changes would go into place even if the economics of the current Luxury Tax were pushed out an additional year. Many of the proposed changes today accept parts of proposals by the MLBPA, but again, only if the union for the players accept the cap system, something that is seen as a poison pill by the MLBPA. Earlier Access to Free Agency MLB will accept the MLBPA’s May 27 proposal to reduce the period of reserve to 5 years for 30-year-old players (subject to the Club’s right to sign the player to a one year contract with a salary equal to the average salary of the 125 highest-paid players), decreasing the reserve period below 6 years for the first time since it was introduced in 1976. o 48% of 5 MLS players would have reached free agency a year earlier under this provision during the past CBA. Eliminate Draft Pick Compensation MLB will accept the MLBPA’s May 27 proposal to eliminate the Qualifying Offer system (i.e., signing a free agent will no longer require a team to forfeit draft picks). Increases to Minimum Salaries MLB’s Proposal To Increase The Minimum Salary MLB will increase the minimum salary from $780,000 in 2026 to $1,000,000 in 2027 for players with at least two years of service and $900,000 for players with less than 2 years of service. Players with less than 2 years of service will also earn at least $100,000 under the Pre-Arbitration Bonus Program, bringing their total compensation to at least $1,000,000, if they receive a full year of service (and spend less than half the season on the IL). The league claims that with the players accepting a cap system the increase of the minimum salary to $1,000,000 would be the largest year-over year increase in the minimum salary in Baseball history (and is about $100,000 higher than the previous largest increase). item.title: Chennedy Carter Shares True Feelings After Aces Assistant Coach Mistaken For Her As Becky Hammon Attends JuJu Watkins Game
item.description: May 23, 2026; Las Vegas, Nevada, USA; Las Vegas Aces guard Chennedy Carter (23) dribbles against the Los Angeles Sparks © Imagn Images Chennedy Carter expressed her feelings after a college commentator mistook Las Vegas Aces assistant head coach Nola Henry for Carter. After the 2026 WNBA season, the coaching staff is already scouting for younger talent to strategize for the offseason and the 2027 WNBA draft. However, Carter wasn’t happy with being confused with the Aces coaching staff member. Aces head coach Becky Hammon was also courtside as the USC Trojans defeated the UNLV Lady Rebels, 100-68, as the 2027 WNBA draft’s top prospect, JuJu Watkins, scored 21 points on 9-for-22 from the floor. Henry accompanied Hammon to the game to scout Watkins for the team next season. Notably, the Aces have already traded their 2027 WNBA Draft first-round pick to the Dallas Wings. However, the Aces can still make a deal to bring her to Las Vegas. A user shared on Threads about the commentator mistaking Henry for Carter: “This man calling the USC-UNLV game just identified Nola Henry as Chennedy Carter. 🤣🤣🤣” View on Threads The Texas native was not happy with the user and responded in the comments: “Please don’t mention my name with her or them. How can we get this out there fast enough!?” View on Threads Carter didn’t have a cordial farewell in Las Vegas, as she was waived just before her non-guaranteed veteran minimum contract was set to be converted into a guaranteed deal. This might have irked Carter, and she didn’t hold back on social media. She is known for being one of the more vocal players in the WNBA. The Aces Congratulate The 2026 WNBA Champions The Aces also congratulated the 2026 WNBA champions, the Golden State Valkyries, after the latter defeated the Atlanta Dream in seven games. Gabby Williams was awarded the Finals MVP after Game 7, as the Valkyries won 68-63. The Aces’ team account commented on their win in a post on X: “Congrats, Champs! 👏✨” The Aces were ousted by the Valkyries in three games in the semifinals. The former might look to improve the roster in the offseason after their core fell to the Valkyries’ defense. Though A’ja Wilson had another MVP season, the team couldn’t hold on in the postseason. item.title: United ease troubles with sensational Roma comeback, PSG rampant in Champions League
item.description: Manchester United's Brazilian striker Matheus Cunha scored twice to give his team a Champions League win over Roma (Oli SCARFF) Manchester United fought back from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday to hand beleaguered manager Michael Carrick a reprieve, while holders Paris Saint-Germain continued their perfect start in the competition by hitting Villarreal for six. Looking set for another abject defeat when two behind within 18 minutes through a smart Mathias Soule finish and Donyell Malen's penalty, United staged a thrilling comeback in the second half to turn a poisonous atmosphere at Old Trafford to one of joy. Matheus Cunha, who was sent off in stoppage time, saved the day for United with a brace in three minutes with the final whistle nearing, sparking wild celebrations in the stands. Those scenes at the end of the game couldn't have been more different to the anger which pulsated around the ground in the first half, when United fans threw tennis balls and other objects onto the Old Trafford pitch and directed foul-mouthed chants at the club's majority owners, the Glazer family. "We knew that the fans would be behind us until the last day, we just had to get a result for them," United captain Bruno Fernandes told TNT. United head into Sunday's match with Aston Villa, beaten 3-0 at Barcelona, in an entirely different mood after punishing slapdash Roma who vanished in the second half after having shown why they look like league title contenders in Italy. "I spoke at half-time about being positive. Anything can happen here, I've seen it many times over the years," said Carrick. "You just need something to go our way and the boys were fantastic second half." Roma, who also threw away a commanding lead against Real Madrid in their only other defeat of the season, failed to deal a knockout blow and crumbled once Bruno Fernandes pulled United back into the game in the 58th minute at the second time of asking from the penalty spot. The Portuguese thumped home past Roma's third-choice goalkeeper Devis Vasquez, who saved the first attempt but was let down by his teammates encroaching in the penalty area. And that set up Cunha to hit Roma with a one-two that decided a thrilling encounter and gave Carrick some breathing room with the international break coming up after the weekend. - Perfect PSG - PSG were in ruthless mood even without star player Khvicha Kvaratskhelia as they beat Villarreal 6-0 on a night in which Europe's elite clubs paid tribute to tragic Tenerife player Jesus de Miguel with a moment's silence before kick-offs. De Miguel died aged 30 from injuries he suffered in a sickening collision with FC Andorra's goalkeeper in a Spanish second-division match, leaving football in mourning and condolences pouring in from around the globe. "You just need something to go our way and the boys were fantastic second half." Roma, who also threw away a commanding lead against Real Madrid in their only other defeat of the season, failed to deal a knockout blow and crumbled once Bruno Fernandes pulled United back into the game in the 58th minute at the second time of asking from the penalty spot. And that set up Cunha to hit Roma with a one-two that decided a thrilling encounter and gave Carrick some breathing room with the international break coming up after the weekend. - Perfect PSG - PSG were in ruthless mood even without star player Khvicha Kvaratskhelia as they beat Villarreal 6-0 on a night in which Europe's elite clubs paid tribute to tragic Tenerife player Jesus de Miguel with a moment's silence before kick-offs. De Miguel died aged 30 from injuries he suffered in a sickening collision with FC Andorra's goalkeeper in a Spanish second-division match, leaving football in mourning and condolences pouring in from around the globe. PSG tore into sorry Villarreal, with Joao Neves, Desire Doue, Senny Mayulu and Fabian Ruiz all striking in eight first-half minutes as the French outfit set a record for the fastest four goals scored in a match in Europe's elite club competition. It certainly didn't look like PSG were missing Kvaratskhelia, Ousmane Dembele, captain Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes, and further strikes from Spain World Cup star Ruiz and teenager David Boly rounded off a stellar performance which put Luis Enrique's team top of the table. "We were impressive throughout and we are really pleased even if it is very difficult for Villarreal," said Luis Enrique. "But it is hard when you play against a team like us that presses constantly." Another team missing a host of stars in Bayern Munich saw off Atletico Madrid 2-0 to move into the top eight positions. Teenage Germany forward Lennart Karl and Konrad Laimer netted in the second half in Madrid as Bayern triumphed despite the absence of Jamal Musiala, Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari. Inter Milan recovered from derby defeat at the weekend with a comfortable 3-0 win over Feyenoord which came through goals from Yann Bisseck, Pio Esposito and Piotr Zielinski. td/lp

item.title: Pittsburgh Steelers 2026 Schedule, Week-By-Week Analysis
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers players before a playoff game against the Houston Texans on Jan. 12, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Pittsburgh Steelers will have a new look in 2026, with a new head coach and more as change unfolds around the historic organization. With the Steelers winning the AFC North in 2025, they’ll also be facing a first-place schedule for the first time since 2021. PITTSBURGH STEELERS 2026 SCHEDULE Week 1: Sunday, Sept. 13, 1 p.m. vs. Atlanta Falcons, FOX, 20-13 W Week 2: Sunday, Sept. 20, 1 p.m. at New England Patriots, CBS, 20-3 L Week 3: Sunday, Sept. 27, 1 p.m. vs. Cincinnati Bengals, CBS, 30-27 W Week 4: Thursday, Oct. 1, 8:15 p.m. at Cleveland Browns, Amazon, 27-24 L Week 5: Sunday, Oct. 11, 1 p.m. vs. Indianapolis Colts, CBS, 34-22 W Week 6: Sunday, Oct. 19, 1 p.m. at Tampa Bay Buccaneers, CBS, 26-19 W (OT) Week 7: Sunday, Oct. 25, 9:30 a.m. vs. New Orleans Saints at Paris, France, NFLN, W 16-10 Week 8: Sunday, Nov. 1, 1 p.m. vs. Cleveland Browns, CBS, W 27-6 Week 9: BYE Week 10: Sunday, Nov. 15, 8:20 p.m. at Cincinnati Bengals, NBC Week 11: Sunday, Nov. 22, 4:25 p.m. at Philadelphia Eagles, CBS Week 12: Friday, Nov. 27, 3 p.m. vs. Denver Broncos, Amazon Week 13: Sunday, Dec. 6, 8:20 p.m. vs. Houston Texans, NBC Week 14: Monday, Dec. 14, 8:15 p.m. at Jacksonville Jaguars, ESPN Week 15: Sunday, Dec. 20, 1 p.m. vs. Baltimore Ravens, CBS Week 16: Sat/Sun, Dec. 26/27, TBD vs. Carolina Panthers, TBD Week 17: Sunday, Jan. 3, 1 p.m. at Tennessee Titans, CBS Week 18: Sat/Sun, Jan 9/10, TBD at Baltimore Ravens, TBD Preseason Week 1: Thursday, Aug. 13, 7 p.m. vs. Green Bay Packers, KDKA, 28-9 W Preseason Week 2: Friday, Aug. 21, 7 p.m. vs New York Jets, KDKA, 17-0 L Preseason Week 3: Thursday, Aug. 27, 7 p.m. at Buffalo Bills, KDKA, 28-27 L PITTSBURGH STEELERS 2026 SCHEDULE ANALYSIS WEEK 10: Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals, Sunday, Nov. 15, 8:20 p.m., NBC Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow in a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Dec. 1, 2024. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Steelers head to Cincinnati with painful memories from their last trip to Paycor Stadium, where Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins fueled an offensive explosion in prime time. One possible silver lining for Pittsburgh: this matchup won’t feature a Mike Tomlin–led team on Thursday Night Football, a setting that has historically been unforgiving. It will, however, feature Tomlin, as the former Steelers coach will be in the building for NBC’s Football Night in America pregame show, his debut broadcast with his former team. WEEK 11: Pittsburgh Steelers at Philadelphia Eagles, Sunday, Nov. 22, 4:25 p.m., CBS Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. lines up against Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Jahan Dotson on Dec. 16, 2024. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Keystone Clash returns to Philadelphia, where history is firmly against Pittsburgh. Jalen Hurts has never lost to the Steelers, and Pittsburgh has not won in Philadelphia since 1965.

PITTSBURGH STEELERS 2026 SCHEDULE Week 1: Sunday, Sept. 13, 1 p.m. vs. Atlanta Falcons, FOX, 20-13 W Week 2: Sunday, Sept. 20, 1 p.m. at New England Patriots, CBS, 20-3 L Week 3: Sunday, Sept. 27, 1 p.m. vs. Cincinnati Bengals, CBS, 30-27 W Week 4: Thursday, Oct. 1, 8:15 p.m. at Cleveland Browns, Amazon, 27-24 L Week 5: Sunday, Oct. 11, 1 p.m. vs. Indianapolis Colts, CBS, 34-22 W Week 6: Sunday, Oct. 19, 1 p.m. at Tampa Bay Buccaneers, CBS, 26-19 W (OT) Week 7: Sunday, Oct. 25, 9:30 a.m. vs. New Orleans Saints at Paris, France, NFLN, W 16-10 Week 8: Sunday, Nov. 1, 1 p.m. vs. Cleveland Browns, CBS, W 27-6 Week 9: BYE Week 10: Sunday, Nov. 15, 8:20 p.m. at Cincinnati Bengals, NBC Week 11: Sunday, Nov. 22, 4:25 p.m. at Philadelphia Eagles, CBS Week 12: Friday, Nov. 27, 3 p.m. vs. Denver Broncos, Amazon Week 13: Sunday, Dec. 6, 8:20 p.m. vs. Houston Texans, NBC Week 14: Monday, Dec. 14, 8:15 p.m. at Jacksonville Jaguars, ESPN Week 15: Sunday, Dec. 20, 1 p.m. vs. Baltimore Ravens, CBS Week 16: Sat/Sun, Dec. 26/27, TBD vs. Carolina Panthers, TBD Week 17: Sunday, Jan. 3, 1 p.m. at Tennessee Titans, CBS Week 18: Sat/Sun, Jan 9/10, TBD at Baltimore Ravens, TBD Preseason Week 1: Thursday, Aug. 13, 7 p.m. vs. Green Bay Packers, KDKA, 28-9 W Preseason Week 2: Friday, Aug. 21, 7 p.m. vs New York Jets, KDKA, 17-0 L Preseason Week 3: Thursday, Aug. 27, 7 p.m. at Buffalo Bills, KDKA, 28-27 L PITTSBURGH STEELERS 2026 SCHEDULE ANALYSIS WEEK 10: Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals, Sunday, Nov. 15, 8:20 p.m., NBC Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow in a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Dec. 1, 2024. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Steelers head to Cincinnati with painful memories from their last trip to Paycor Stadium, where Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins fueled an offensive explosion in prime time. One possible silver lining for Pittsburgh: this matchup won’t feature a Mike Tomlin–led team on Thursday Night Football, a setting that has historically been unforgiving. It will, however, feature Tomlin, as the former Steelers coach will be in the building for NBC’s Football Night in America pregame show, his debut broadcast with his former team. WEEK 11: Pittsburgh Steelers at Philadelphia Eagles, Sunday, Nov. 22, 4:25 p.m., CBS Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. lines up against Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Jahan Dotson on Dec. 16, 2024. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Keystone Clash returns to Philadelphia, where history is firmly against Pittsburgh. Jalen Hurts has never lost to the Steelers, and Pittsburgh has not won in Philadelphia since 1965. A road win here would be well outside the norm and one of the more surprising results on the schedule. WEEK 12: Denver Broncos at Pittsburgh Steelers, Friday, Nov. 27, 3 p.m., Amazon Prime Pittsburgh Steelers outside linebacker T.J. Watt rushes against Denver Broncos tackle Bobby Massie on Oct. 10, 2021. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Pittsburgh Steelers will host the Denver Broncos on Black Friday, the first time the Steelers have ever played on the day after Thanksgiving. The game will be streamed via Amazon Prime , and will also be available over-the-air in the Pittsburgh market, on a station to be named at a later date. It will mark just the sixth time the Steelers have played on a Friday, and the first time since 1946. The Steelers were 3-2 in five all-time Friday games, with their last game a 14-7 home win over the Chicago Cardinals at Forbes Field to open the 1946 season on Sept. 20. The NFL has traditionally set aside Friday nights for high school football and that was codified into law via the Sports Broadcasting Act of 1961, which prohibits the NFL from broadcasting games after 6 p.m. on Friday nights or Saturdays between the second Friday in September and the second Saturday in December,. That’s why the Black Friday game must kick off at 3 p.m., but with the day after Thanksgiving a day off for many Americans, the NFL and Amazon Prime Video decided to pursue playing a game during the day. The first Black Friday game was in 2023, when the Miami Dolphins beat the New York Jets. The Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Las Vegas Raiders in 2024 and the Chicago Bears beat the Philadelphia Eagles last season. The Steelers last faced the Broncos in 2024, when they went on the road for a 13-7 win Denver. The last game between the teams at Acrisure Stadium was a 27-19 Steelers win in 2021. Pittsburgh has won the last three games between the teams overall. WEEK 13: Houston Texans at Pittsburgh Steelers, Sunday, Dec. 6, 8:20 p.m, NBC Pittsburgh Steelers nose tackle Keeanu Benton hits Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud on Jan. 12, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now This matchup carries a bitter edge. The Houston Texans eliminated the Steelers in the Wild Card round less than a season ago, winning 30–6 in what ultimately became Mike Tomlin’s final game as head coach. With that loss still fresh, it’s hard to imagine this game won’t feel personal for Pittsburgh. The game will also feature Tomlin on the NBC Football Night in America broadcast crew live in Pittsburgh. WEEK 14: Pittsburgh Steelers at Jacksonville Jaguars, Monday, Dec. 15, 8:15 p.m., ESPN Pittsburgh Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson in a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Aug. 9, 2025 — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Steelers travel to Jacksonville to face Trevor Lawrence, who is 1–0 against Pittsburgh after a rain-soaked win at Acrisure Stadium in 2022. Prior to that, the Steelers had won their previous two games in Duval, including a historic comeback led by Ben Roethlisberger in 2018. New coach Liam Coen will be eager to rewrite Jacksonville’s uneven home history against Pittsburgh. WEEK 15: Baltimore Ravens at Pittsburgh Steelers, Sunday, Dec. 20, 1 p.m., CBS Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey tries to tackle Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren on Jan. 4, 2026,. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Steelers will host the Baltimore Ravens in what is almost always one of the NFL’s most physical matchups. The last time these two met in Pittsburgh, the game carried massive implications, a winner-take-all showdown for the AFC North. Pittsburgh emerged victorious after a heartbreaking missed field goal by Ravens kicker Tyler Loop, a moment that still stings in Baltimore and fuels the rivalry even further. WEEK 16: Carolina Panthers at Pittsburgh Steelers, Date/Time TBD Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth looks for a call against the Carolina Panthers on Aug. 21, 2025. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now History is firmly stacked against the Carolina Panthers. Carolina has never defeated the Steelers in Pittsburgh and hasn’t beaten Pittsburgh anywhere since 1996, the only win in franchise history against them. Still, after a season in which the Panthers nearly upset Matthew Stafford’s Rams in the playoffs, a revamped Carolina team led by Bryce Young could arrive eager to finally make history. This game will be played on either Saturday, Dec. 26 or Sunday, Dec. 27. WEEK 17: Pittsburgh Steelers at Tennessee Titans, Sunday, Jan. 3., 1 p.m., CBS Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren carries the ball in a game against the Tennessee Titans on Nov. 2, 2023. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Pittsburgh enters Nashville looking to continue its recent success against the Tennessee Titans. The Steelers’ last trip to Nissan Stadium resulted in a 27–24 win in 2020, when former Steelers offensive coordinator Arthur Smith was calling plays for Tennessee. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. item.content:encoded: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. Tackling, leverage issues persist OSU showed a vulnerability early, but against Houston and Texas Tech it was understandable in terms of talent and timing on the schedule. Tackling improved over the prior five games, but opponents’ speed also dropped. Against legitimate athletic threats, the Beavers showed their tackling fundamentals, speed, strength and angles are still areas of weakness. 7. The areas for Braden Atkinson to develop are clear Entz detailed Atkinson’s reliance on his first read and susceptibility to being impacted by pass rush when it’s not there. Of course, a defense has to have the talent and ability to do something about it. Atkinson’s ceiling is high provided he develops in his reading of progressions, grows more comfortable checking into run plays and finds effective counters to the better defenses OSU faces. 8. Caleb Ojeda came up big Ojeda’s three field goals should not get lost to the box score, particularly with a 54-yarder. At 14-9, if OSU manages to make a stop and gain momentum, the game could have changed and the importance of Ojeda’s kicks becomes paramount to the game. 9. Kickoff coverage remains a problem As the sample size for OSU’s kickoffs grows, so too does the success opponents continue to have. To allow a 44-yard kickoff return following a 14-play drive that spanned more than five minutes is inexcusable. OSU would literally have been better off kicking out of bounds, which has been enough of an issue as well. The Beavers rank 114th in average kickoff return yards allowed and 126th on a per game basis. 10. The weakness at corner is glaring Without belaboring a point that’s been stated on nearly a weekly basis, the matchup disadvantage at No. 2 corner remains the Achilles’ heel for the defense. Against bigger receivers like Freeman it’s simply a matter of when, not if, they will haul in big catches. Read the original article on oregonlive.com . item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said. He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring. Latest Beavers news Justin Joyner wins first game as Oregon State coach in blowout Atkinson, Legree join Nike’s Blue Ribbon Elite as OSU extends apparel deal Pac-12 confirms play clock error led to penalty on Oregon State in its loss to Fresno State At 6-foot-4 and 245 pounds, Comer was dominating in junior college from his athleticism alone. He didn’t know the finer points of playing football. Hand placement, setting the edge in the run game and pass coverage were not in his repertoire. Comer was there to pin his ears back and attack the quarterback, regardless of the down and distance. “They didn’t ask much of me,” Comer said. “They told me just do what I do, use my athleticism, get to the quarterback.” What Comer lacks in experience, he makes up for in ability. He consistently ranks among OSU’s fastest players in practice, which was invaluable to a team seeking more pass rush. “His athleticism is off the charts,” defensive coordinator Mike MacIntyre said. “We see him grow leaps and bounds. Playing a lot more (against Montana), he will grow leaps and bounds going into this Saturday because now he’s seen it, it slows down, he understands the different things.” RELATED: Experts release Oregon State vs. UTEP predictions, best bets, and preview for Week 4 Comer has 10 tackles thus far, including four in each of the past two games, and is already more than a situational pass rusher for the Beavers. He credits MacIntyre and edge coaches Joe Seumalo and George Frazier with helping him learn the game, particularly pass coverage. Ideally, pairing Comer with Takari Hickle will allow OSU to generate more pressure as teams won’t be able to focus all their offensive line on one side. “Teams have to respect his speed,” Hickle said. “If they don’t, then he’ll run right by them. He is definitely a threat in coverage and in the pass game.” Oregon State (1-2) at UTEP (1-2) When: Saturday, Sept. 26 Time: 6 p.m. PT Where: Sun Bowl, El Paso, Texas Betting line: Oregon State by 10.5 TV: MW+ (Mountain West Plus) On air: KEX 1190 in Portland, KEJO 1240 and 93.7 in Corvallis Stream : You c

item.title: Lake Mary breaks through First Coast blockade in Region 1-3A golf
item.description: Lake Mary crashed the First Coast party in Port Orange. Led by co-medalist Riley Sillaway with a 3-under 69, the Rams won the FHSAA boys Region 1-3A golf tournament on Nov. 2 at the Golf Club at Cypress Head, nosing out Ponte Vedra by one shot at 6-over-par 294. Tocoi Creek and Spruce Creek tied for third, another four shots back. Beachside was fifth, six shots off the lead and Creekside sixth, nine shots back. Ponte Vedra entered the tournament first among Class 3A teams in the state on the iWanamaker rankings, while Lake Mary was fourth and Tocoi Creek fifth. Beachside was seventh and finished second to the Toros in the District 3-3A tournament last week. The stage was set for a First Coast domination but the Rams, who have won five state championships in the highest division since 2004, had other idea.s The one-stroke difference between the Rams and Sharks could be found in the early holes at Cypress Head. The four players whose score counted for Lake Mary played the first four holes at 1-under and Ponte Vedra's four played them at 4-over. James Nagle, Maxwell Morgan and Jake Mason tied as low Sharks players at 1-over 73. Carson Perry of Spruce Creek tied Sillaway for medalist. Ambrose Kinnare of Tocoi Creek, Charlie Hipp of Creekside and Vishruth Badiga of Lake Mary tied for third at 1-under 71. Based on the iWanamaker rankings, Beachside and Creekside should reach the Class 3A state tournament Nov. 13-14 at the Mission Inn Resort in Howey-in-the-Hills as at-large teams, with Nease another possibility. The state tournament field will be finalized next week. Lily Wachter eagle-two caps big day for Beachside Freshman Lily Wachter drove the green of the par-4 17th hole and drained a 17-foot putt for eagle to play five holes at 4-under and finish with a 67 at the Hawkstone Country Club in Gainesville to lead the Barracudas to the Region 1-3A team title by two shots over Ponte Vedra. Wachter, who started her round with birdies at Nos. 1, 2 and 4, rallied from a double bogey at the par-5 ninth hole and defeated Nina Santiago of the Sharks by three shots. She drove the 17th green from 236 yards out to set up her eagle putt. Olivia Connell of Beachside tied for fourth with a 72 and Aspen Bikowski of Bartram Trail finished sixth with a 73. Boys regional roundup: Bolles outlasts Providence All five Bolles players shot 77 or lower and the Bulldogs won the Region 1-1A tournament at the King & Bear by nine shots over Providence. Nico Vasto led the Bulldogs with a 74 and Brendan Walrath added a 75. Ethan Grossman led Providence with a 73, tying Brody Mitchell of Maclay for second individually. Hunter Glantz of Florida High was the medalist with a 70. … Live Oak Suwannee's Ty Hurst was the Region 1-2A medalist with a 67 at the Fort Walton Beach Country Club on Nov. 2 and the Bulldogs finished second by 13 shots to Gulf Breeze. Girls regional roundup: Sophia Moody on fire Fleming Island sophomore Sophia Moody shot 4-under 32 on the front nine at the Quail Heights Country Club in Lake City and went on to win the Region 1-2A individual title with a 6-under 65 on Nov. 3. She defeated Lily Martin of South Walton Beach Santa Rosa by one shot and Lily Chiang of Stanton by three. Santa Rosa (305) won the team title by 24 shots over Stanton. … Moody is a combined 11-under in the first two rounds of the postseason and she has shot 69, 66, 67 and 66 in her last four 18-hole rounds. … The Bolles girls got three players in the 70s and won the Region 1-1A tournament on Nov. 2 at Eagle Harbor by 21 shots over Providence. Chloe McGrath led the Bulldogs to their 11th tournament victory of the season with a 73. Sahana Chokshi of Episcopal birdied her first three holes and went on to win the individual title with a 4-under 68 to assure her a spot in the Class 1A state tournament Nov. 17-18. It's the second year in a row she has won or tied as region medalist. Providence was led by Honor Donaldson, who finished second to Chokshi with a 71 that included an eagle at the par-5 12th hole. … Weather has delayed the Region 2-1A tournament at the Cocoa Beach Country Club to Nov. 6. Aubrey Brooks of Keystone Heights is playing as an individual. item.title: MN Vikings Clearing Roster Room for Possible Move?
item.description: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect After their first loss on Sunday against the Detroit Lions , everything is on the table for the Minnesota Vikings prior to the trade deadline. They are 6-1 , but the offense remains a massive question. Kevin O’Connell has stuck behind Kyler Murray as his quarterback, but that doesn’t mean other changes aren’t on the horizon. For now, though, the status quo remains in play, and Minnesota will soon turn its focus to the 6-1 Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football. The long week gives general manager Nolan Teasley additional time to bring in talent, but he hasn’t pulled the trigger on anything yet. That didn’t stop the MN Vikings from opening spots on their roster. Trevor Keegan among Minnesota Vikings sent packing We are still a week from the NFL trade deadline, but that doesn’t preclude teams from making moves ahead of time. So far the Minnesota Vikings have been linked to plenty of big names but have done nothing of consequence. On Tuesday, though, they opened a pair of roster spots by cutting both (G) Trevor Keegan and (TE) Bryson Nesbit. The Vikings waived G Trevor Keegan — who they signed at the roster cutdown deadline before the season — and released TE Bryson Nesbit from the practice squad. Guard depth in an interesting spot. Only have third-rounder Caleb Tiernan. — Alec Lewis (@alec_lewis) November 3, 2026 Related: New Vikings GM Grinding the Phones in Search of Trade Trevor Keegan might be most notable for his influencer wife Hanna Cavinder , a former Miami Hurricanes basketball player. The MN Vikings claimed him off waivers from the Dallas Cowboys as guard depth, and he played in seven games , but he will be looking for a new team quickly. Teasley making room for new acquisitions…? Guard depth isn’t ideal for the Vikings right now with Donovan Jackson out for the year and Will Fries struggling. Their willingness to move on , though, could suggest something is on the horizon, as speculated by beat writer Emily Leiker (Star Tribune) . Seem to be making roster space… — emily leiker (@emleiker) November 3, 2026 It’s going to be a very interesting week for the Minnesota Vikings. Should general manager Nolan Teasley make moves of consequence over the next week, this team could vault right back into Super Bowl contention. How the vacated roster spots are utilized will be the story of the next couple of weeks. Read more at Minnesota Sports Fan

item.title: Raphinha, Yamal power Barca to Champions League win over Villa
item.description: Lamine Yamal and Raphinha got the goals as Barcelona beat Aston Villa in the Champions League on Tuesday (Josep LAGO) Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa on Tuesday, ending the English side's perfect start to the competition. Five-time winners Barcelona took an early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued his fine goalscoring form with a second-half brace. Barca bounced back after defeat by champions Paris Saint-Germain in their previous European outing to stay in the hunt for a top eight league phase berth. Unai Emery's Villa competed well in the first half but were eventually undone by Barca's greater ability in the final third. The Champions League anthem was not played before the game, as a mark of respect for Tenerife striker Jesus De Miguel, who died on Tuesday morning after an on-pitch collision in a Spanish second division match the previous day, provoking shock across the football world. "Yes it was (a good win), I want to dedicate this win to the fans, but today I don't want to talk about football, I want to send a message to the family of Jesus -- may he rest in peace," Raphinha told Movistar. "This can happen to anyone, it's very tough... you're going to play a game and the same thing can happen to you... "From the club, I want to send a message of strength to the family." Villa captain John McGinn had only visited the Camp Nou once previously, on a summer holiday as an eight-year-old, and might have expected better weather than the downpour both teams were subjected to. The skipper might also have expected a more focused start, with Villa handing Barcelona the lead in the seventh minute. The Spanish champions pressed Aston Villa extremely high and Joao Gomes played a poor pass straight to Yamal in his own box. The 19-year-old winger gladly took the gift and stroked past Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. "Tonight was a huge learning curve for us and I am sure it will stand us in good stead for the future," McGinn told TNT Sports. "Barcelona made the right decisions at the right times and scored really good goals." Yamal's goal was his 14th in the competition across his career, beating Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe's previous record tally of 13 netted as a teenager in the Champions League. Emery, who endured one of the worst nights of his career away at Barca when helming PSG in 2017 during a 6-1 defeat, may have feared the worst. However Villa reacted strongly and Matty Cash had a vicious drive deflected narrowly wide before Joao Cancelo blocked Gomes's effort. - End-to-end - Suzuki saved from Anthony Gordon as Villa again struggled to bring the ball out from the back under Barca's pressing. Garcia was called into action again by Johan Manzambi as the match lurched from end-to-end. Barcelona extended their lead early in the second half when Fermin Lopez fed Raphinha, who showed quick footwork before finding the bottom corner. Cancelo set up Raphinha for Barcelo

Garcia was called into action again by Johan Manzambi as the match lurched from end-to-end. Barcelona extended their lead early in the second half when Fermin Lopez fed Raphinha, who showed quick footwork before finding the bottom corner. Cancelo set up Raphinha for Barcelona's third with a superb cross with the outside of his boot. The Brazil winger, who has made the number nine position his own this season, pounced from close range for his 19th goal across all competitions. Yamal sent a shot skidding wide as Barcelona probed for a fourth. It did not come, but the Catalan giants were able to record a first Champions League clean sheet in 19 games. Flick was pleased with Barcelona keeping Villa at bay. "It was important that we defended together very compactly," said the German coach. "The back line played on an amazing level, they defended everything." Aston Villa are well positioned, provisionally third in the league phase table. Emery said the match was a good lesson for his side against one of the biggest teams in Europe. "We must be ruthless in the attacking third, we must be more demanding of ourselves, creating those chances to score," Emery told reporters. "The 3-0 is maybe more (heavy) than we deserved, but we accept this defeat, taking a lot of information for our improvement." rbs/lp/td

item.title: How rested UTSA aims to stay sharp at Florida Atlantic
item.description: UTSA Roadrunners celebrate after defeating South Florida at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas on Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) With a little extra time to recover as UTSA enjoyed an 11-day break between games, safety Elijah Newell said he savored some quiet moments at home, cooking up steaks and watching football as a fan. The Roadrunners entered the open date 7-1 overall and 4-0 in the American Conference, and Traylor said he was on alert to ensure a sense of complacency didn't start to creep in. Even in restful moments, Newell said he remains driven by memories of UTSA's struggles during 7-6 seasons the past two years. The Roadrunners returned to work after their brief break with the same steady practice habits they've shown all season, Traylor said, but the real test of how UTSA handled the open week will arrive in a matchup against Florida Atlantic at 6:30 p.m. Thursday in Boca Raton, Fla. "I hope we're desperate and not prosperous," Traylor said. "I hope we don't sit around and read all of our press clippings, and believe we're really that good." UTSA Roadrunners quarterback Owen McCown runs the ball in a game against South Florida at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas on Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) The Roadrunners wouldn't have to look very hard to find fuel for their egos. The 7-1 start is UTSA's best since 2023, and the team is receiving top-25 votes in both the coaches and Associated Press polls. The team's five-game winning streak is the longest since 2023, and UTSA stands as one of just two teams with unbeaten records in American competition, joining North Texas. But quarterback Owen McCown, who said he took advantage of some extra time during the open week to visit family, said the team returned as ready as ever to get back to work. "Just can't buy into the outside noise," McCown said. "I know there's a lot of talk right now, and our record's really good, but you have to look at it like you're 0-0." UTSA vs. FAU: 5 players to watch as Roadrunners look for another road win Traylor said he keeps the Roadrunners sharp by emphasizing that any of their four one-score wins could've ended differently, or by harping on mistakes like three lost turnovers and three pre-snap penalties in UTSA's most recent 42-19 win at Tulane. Still, he's aimed to take some of the physical pressure off the players through this period, holding practices without pads while focusing on fundamentals and technique. Though the Roadrunners have avoided many major injuries this year, Traylor said much of the roster is "limping home." "We needed it just for our own mental and physical well-being right now," Traylor said. "If you can make it through your first eight games, which we did, and get a bye right now, it's about the perfect time to get one." The Roadrunners are also heading into the time of the year that has typically been their best, as UTSA is 18-5 in November during Traylor's tenure. McC

"If you can make it through your first eight games, which we did, and get a bye right now, it's about the perfect time to get one." The Roadrunners are also heading into the time of the year that has typically been their best, as UTSA is 18-5 in November during Traylor's tenure. McCown said the biggest key is newcomers and first-time starters developing a feel for the team, and the results have already started to show. item.title: There’s 1 NFL Hall of Fame QB who should replace Troy Aikman on MNF
item.description: The future of Troy Aikman on ESPN’s Monday Night Football broadcast has become one of the biggest sports media stories of the NFL season. With Aikman’s contract set to expire after Super Bowl LXI on February 14, 2027, speculation about his replacement is heating up. While several names have been mentioned, there is one candidate who makes more sense than anyone else: Peyton Manning. MORE: NFL power rankings entering Week 9: All 32 teams ranked worst to first Peyton Manning is the obvious choice to replace Troy Aikman Oct 17, 2019; Denver, CO, USA; FOX Sports broadcaster Troy Aikman before the game between the Denver Broncos and the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-USA TODAY Sports Credit: USA TODAY Sports (Reuters) There has been plenty of discussion about who ESPN could bring in to replace Aikman if he leaves the network. Greg Olsen has emerged as a popular candidate, while Jason Kelce could also be an option given his existing role on the Monday Night Countdown panel. Tony Romo is another name that could generate plenty of attention. The former Cowboys quarterback recently became available after parting ways with CBS. Replacing one Dallas quarterback with another would certainly be an interesting storyline, but Romo is not the answer. Instead, ESPN should make a serious push to bring Manning into the traditional Monday Night Football booth. The Hall of Fame quarterback already has an established relationship with ESPN through the ManningCast, which he hosts alongside his brother, Eli Manning. The alternate broadcast has become a familiar part of ESPN’s Monday Night Football coverage, giving Peyton plenty of experience discussing NFL games in front of a national audience. Manning also brings the credibility, personality, football knowledge, and name recognition that ESPN should want in its lead NFL broadcast booth. Pairing him with Joe Buck would give the network an opportunity to create another high-profile broadcasting partnership. MORE: NFL contenders & pretenders after Week 8 ESPN should make Peyton Manning its top priority Peyton Manning in field before Miami Dolphins and the Indianapolis Colts game. Credit: Grace Hollars-USA TODAY Network via Imagn Images. There is no shortage of potential candidates, but Manning should be at the top of ESPN’s list. Greg Olsen is a legitimate option, and his past experience as Fox’s lead analyst (before Tom Brady) makes him an attractive candidate. However, Olsen doesn’t bring the same combination of Hall of Fame playing experience, national recognition, and existing ESPN relationship as Manning. The biggest obstacle could be convincing Manning to take on the traditional broadcast role. He has previously declined opportunities to join a regular NFL broadcast booth, and his current arrangement with ESPN allows him to work alongside Eli without the demands of traveling to every game. ESPN would have to make an offer compelling enough to change that. Still,

item.title: Manchester United fans force Champions League game delay with protest against ownership
item.description: Manchester United fans protested against the team's ownership on Tuesday -Credit:Michael Regan, Getty Images Manchester United fans demonstrated against the club's owners both before and during their match against AS Roma on Tuesday. A group of United supporters began hurling tennis balls and other items onto the Old Trafford pitch. The action commenced at 20 minutes and five seconds, a timeframe chosen to symbolize the year the Glazers took control at Old Trafford. Hero of the night Matheus Cunha was among the players who assisted in clearing the objects from the playing surface. After they were removed, the match was able to continue, as per the Manchester Evening News . Soccer star Jesús de Miguel tragically dies aged 30 after mid-game collision as tributes paid Goalkeeper involved in tragic Jesús de Miguel collision 'breaks down' after soccer star's death -Credit:Michael Regan, Getty Images Hundreds of yellow and green balloons were also launched from the Stretford End before kickoff as the teams emerged from the tunnel. The demonstration marks the latest in an extended series of protests against United's ownership. Before the Manchester derby on September 13, approximately 500 fans rallied against the club's efforts to eliminate ticket touting. United had anticipated the initiative would end ticket touting, and although the operation was considered successful, they also acknowledged that "some innocent supporters may have been affected". Chants opposing Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers have become a fixture of the United repertoire, with fans directing their frustration at the team's woeful performance toward the owners rather than Michael Carrick. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE However, for the first time since September 10, United fans were given good reason to cheer on their side on Tuesday, coming back from 2-0 down at halftime to beat Roma 3-2. The comeback began courtesy of a Bruno Fernandes penalty, before Cunha equalized with a close-range effort in the 83rd minute thanks in no small part to woeful defending from the visitors. The Brazilian then gave United the lead three minutes later with a thundering effort, prompting him to take off his jersey and dive into the crowd in celebration, leading to a yellow card. This proved costly as the clock wound down, with a rash tackle in the 91st minute leading to a second yellow as the hero of the game was given his marching orders. Regardless, United were able to hold onto the lead and thus end their nine-game winless run.

item.title: High school football: 6A quarterfinal previews
item.description: Mountain Ridge and Herriman play a high school football game in Herriman on Friday, Oct. 2, 2026. | Scott G Winterton, Deseret News 6A Quarterfinals No. 5 Davis (8-3) at No. 4 Herriman (9-2) 6A quarterfinals Friday, Nov. 6, 4 p.m. Parry’s Power Guide: Davis by 4 All-time series: Herriman leads 2-1 (since 2019) Last meeting: Herriman won 35-21 at Davis (Oct. 22, 2021, 6A first round) What Davis needs to do to win Davis has been in this round before. A year ago the Darts were the No. 3 seed and lost 41-38 to Lone Peak in the quarterfinals. This time they’re the lower seed and on the road, but they’re playing better than they were early in the season. Davis started 3-3. Two of those losses came against the top two seeds in 6A: 51-14 to Corner Canyon and 42-7 at Mountain Ridge. The third was 29-21 to American Fork. The Darts have won five straight since then by a combined 201-75. That run includes an outright Region 1 title and last week’s 37-18 first-round win over Farmington. They also beat two 5A quarterfinalists, 56-28 at Fremont and 27-6 at Alta. The two teams’ common opponents can’t separate them. Both lost badly to Mountain Ridge, Davis by 35 and Herriman by 38. Both also routed Weber, Davis 52-6 and Herriman 55-6. Bode Sparrow is the player most likely to swing this game. He scored four touchdowns against Farmington, including a 99-yard kickoff return. He has 62 catches for 882 yards and 18 touchdown catches. He also has four rushing touchdowns and two return touchdowns, and he has 64 tackles on defense.
