item.content:encoded: Mountain Ridge and Herriman play a high school football game in Herriman on Friday, Oct. 2, 2026. | Scott G Winterton, Deseret News 6A Quarterfinals No. 5 Davis (8-3) at No. 4 Herriman (9-2) 6A quarterfinals Friday, Nov. 6, 4 p.m. Parry’s Power Guide: Davis by 4 All-time series: Herriman leads 2-1 (since 2019) Last meeting: Herriman won 35-21 at Davis (Oct. 22, 2021, 6A first round) What Davis needs to do to win Davis has been in this round before. A year ago the Darts were the No. 3 seed and lost 41-38 to Lone Peak in the quarterfinals. This time they’re the lower seed and on the road, but they’re playing better than they were early in the season. Davis started 3-3. Two of those losses came against the top two seeds in 6A: 51-14 to Corner Canyon and 42-7 at Mountain Ridge. The third was 29-21 to American Fork. The Darts have won five straight since then by a combined 201-75. That run includes an outright Region 1 title and last week’s 37-18 first-round win over Farmington. They also beat two 5A quarterfinalists, 56-28 at Fremont and 27-6 at Alta. The two teams’ common opponents can’t separate them. Both lost badly to Mountain Ridge, Davis by 35 and Herriman by 38. Both also routed Weber, Davis 52-6 and Herriman 55-6. Bode Sparrow is the player most likely to swing this game. He scored four touchdowns against Farmington, including a 99-yard kickoff return. He has 62 catches for 882 yards and 18 touchdown catches. He also has four rushing touchdowns and two return touchdowns, and he has 64 tackles on defense. Paden Toula has completed 69.9% of his passes for 1,919 yards and 22 touchdowns. Jaxton Itaaheau has 11 total touchdowns, and Sam Coleman has 50 catches. Coleman also leads the defense with four interceptions and has a defensive touchdown and a return touchdown. To win, Davis has to slow down Filisi Filipe, and that has to start with Ben Dorius (10 sacks) and the front seven. Dexter Frasure leads the team with 83 tackles. Davis’s own running game averages 4.5 yards per carry, so Toula and Sparrow will have to carry the offense. Herriman’s defense has 15 interceptions, so Toula can’t afford mistakes. Davis has won three region titles in four seasons under Scott Peery. The program’s last state title came in 2004. What Herriman needs to do to win Herriman’s plan is to give the ball to Filipe. He has run for 1,542 yards and 27 touchdowns at 9.2 yards per carry, and with three touchdown catches he has 30 total touchdowns. He ran for 134 yards and four touchdowns against Weber last week. Max Stevens adds 557 yards at 7.3 yards per carry. As a team, the Mustangs average 7.6 yards per carry and have 36 rushing touchdowns. Herriman can beat teams in more than one way. Bryson Sweeney has thrown for 1,860 yards and 19 touchdowns with five interceptions, and Hayes Priest leads the team with 46 catches. The Mustangs average 38.3 points per game, third in 6A. They allow 16.3, also third. Their wins include 25-14 over Bountiful, the 5A No. 4 seed and a 5A quarterfinalist, 40-36 at Stansbury, the 4A No. 3 seed, 48-7 at Westlake and 44-0 over Bingham. Their only losses were 22-20 at home to Lehi and 45-7 at unbeaten Mountain Ridge. The defense creates turnovers and big plays. Kemper Castro has 11 sacks, and Ashton Hebert and Aden Jensen have six each, for 28 as a team. Hebert also returned a fumble 39 yards for a touchdown against Weber. Logan Gregory and Aden Perea have four interceptions each. Perea has two defensive touchdowns and Gregory has a return touchdown. Brody Crayk has made four field goals. The concern is close games. Herriman lost to Lehi by two and beat Copper Hills only 23-20, and Davis has the kind of playmakers who can turn a game in a few plays. Herriman also needs to keep Sparrow from breaking a big kick return. The Mustangs lost 22-14 to Mountain Ridge in last year’s quarterfinals, and Matt Rickards’ team is trying to get past this round. The winner plays the Skyridge–American Fork winner. American Fork beat Davis 29-21 in September. Davis statistical breakdown Scoring offense: 33.9 ppg (4th in 6A) Scoring defense: 22.3 ppg (9th in 6A) Passing leader: Paden Toula (158-226, 69.9%, 1,919 yards, 22 TDs, 7 INTs) Rushing leaders: Kysen Gallegos (90 carries, 391 yards, 4 TDs), Briggs Taylor (60 carries, 307 yards, 2 TDs), Jaxton Itaaheau (22 carries, 115 yards, 5 TDs) Receiving leaders: Bode Sparrow (62 rec., 882 yards, 18 TDs), Jaxton Itaaheau (47 rec., 654 yards, 6 TDs), Sam Coleman (50 rec., 521 yards, 2 TDs) Tackles leaders: Dexter Frasure (83 tackles), Ben Dorius (78 tackles), Austin Yeates (72 tackles) Sack leaders: Ben Dorius (10 sacks), Austin Yeates (2 sacks) Interception leaders: Sam Coleman (4 INTs), Cooper Rigby (2 INTs), Porter Hunt (2 INTs) Herriman statistical breakdown Scoring offense: 38.3 ppg (3rd in 6A) Scoring defense: 16.3 ppg (3rd in 6A) Passing leader: Bryson Sweeney (138-243, 56.8%, 1,860 yards, 19 TDs, 5 INTs) Rushing leaders: Filisi Filipe (168 carries, 1,542 yards, 27 TDs), Max Stevens (76 carries, 557 yards, 5 TDs) Receiving leaders: Hayes Priest (46 rec., 551 yards, 4 TDs), Britton Wall (26 rec., 324 yards, 3 TDs) Tackles leaders: Kemper Castro (68 tackles), Gavyn Fox (64 tackles), Ashton Hebert (59 tackles) Sack leaders: Kemper Castro (11 sacks), Ashton Hebert (6 sacks), Aden Jensen (6 sacks) Interception leaders: Logan Gregory (4 INTs), Aden Perea (4 INTs) Skyridge Falcons quarterback Jagger Fountaine (3) throws the ball during a cross-town rivalry high school football game against the Lehi Pioneers at Lehi High School in Lehi on Thursday, Sept. 17, 2026. | Tess Crowley, Deseret News No. 8 American Fork (7-4) at No. 1 Skyridge (9-1) 6A quarterfinals Friday, Nov. 6, 6 p.m. Parry’s Power Guide: Skyridge by 9 All-time series: Skyridge leads 9-1 (since 2019) Last meeting: Skyridge won 21-15 at Skyridge (Oct. 14, 2026, Region 3) What American Fork needs to do to win Nate Childs had six days to get ready. Starter Jake Matsen broke his collarbone early in the Oct. 8 loss to Corner Canyon, and American Fork’s season went to a senior who had started much of last year and had waited behind Matsen this fall. Childs’ first start came on the road at Skyridge, against the No. 1 seed and the team that ended the Cavemen’s season a year ago. The game started badly. Beckham Bennett scored on two short runs in the first quarter, and Skyridge led 14-0. Then American Fork settled in. The Cavemen outscored the Falcons 15-7 the rest of the way. With 8:21 left, Childs threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Zack Cowie and ran in the two-point conversion himself to make it 21-15. That was as close as they got. Last week Childs looked more comfortable. He threw two touchdown passes in a 32-21 first-round win over Copper Hills, and DC Fonua returned an interception 34 yards for a touchdown and later ran for another. Childs now gets a second chance at Skyridge, with three more weeks of first-team snaps than he had in the first meeting. If American Fork avoids another slow start, this rematch could look different. American Fork has beaten good teams this season. It won 29-21 at Davis, the 6A No. 5 seed, and 28-24 at Lone Peak, the No. 7 seed. It also won road games at 5A quarterfinalist Pleasant Grove (36-16) and at Timpview (28-26). The Cavemen’s October slide began with a 20-19 home loss to Lehi on Oct. 2. Matsen got hurt the next week, and the losses to Corner Canyon and Skyridge followed. The defense is American Fork’s best chance. Noah Behm has six interceptions and two defensive touchdowns, and he’s also the second-leading receiver, with four touchdown catches. Dalin Afu has four sacks and two defensive touchdowns, and Sam Thompson has four sacks. Skyridge quarterback Jagger Fountaine has thrown 11 interceptions, so turnovers are American Fork’s clearest path to an upset. Cash Taiese (57 catches, 743 yards, 7 TDs) is Childs’ top target, and Jace Worthington has made nine field goals. There’s a lot of history on the line. Skyri

item.title: George Pickens trade update from NFL insider raises eyebrows after Cowboys loss
item.description: George Pickens trade update from NFL insider raises eyebrows after Cowboys loss originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Cowboys fell in yet another close game on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals , 33-30 in an overtime loss. That puts Dallas at a 3-5 record for the season, which obviously isn't a good look. Heading into their next game against the 2-6 Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, there are a lot of questions about what owner and general manager Jerry Jones may do before the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline. One of the big players that he could possibly move is wide receiver George Pickens. So, will it happen? NFL insider shares latest update on George Pickens trade rumors With all the talk about Pickens possibly getting traded before the trade deadline, one NFL insider is sharing what he's heard. Appearing on the Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said , "I was told the Dallas Cowboys aren't trading George Pickens." Zachary Krueger of NBC Sports adds that Rapoport also said, "As of right now, there's nothing there," as far as a potential trade involving the player. "Pickens, who is playing out the season on the franchise tag, hasn't produced at the level he did in 2025 when he broke out for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns, but he remains a focal point in the offense despite his underwhelming production," Krueger adds. "Pickens still ranks 14th in the league among all receivers in targets and is 12th in total air yards. Despite the Cowboys' disappointing 3-5 record, they remain in the race to win what has been an underwhelming NFC East." He adds, "With team owner Jerry Jones saying earlier that Pickens needs to be targeted more, it's safe to assume he will remain with the Cowboys for the season." So, all of that talk and buzz about Pickens getting moved may amount to nothing. But never say never until Nov. 10 has come and gone. More NFL news: Caleb Williams incident leads to Patriots player punishment from the NFL Giants' Cam Skattebo is in trouble with the NFL Maxx Crosby trade update is significant news for Lions, Bears and Cowboys

item.title: Details emerge following crash that killed 2 Texas Lutheran football players
item.description: Texas Lutheran University will hold a memorial on November 5 for two student-athletes killed in a Seguin crash on State Highway 46. (NurPhoto via Getty Images) Texas Lutheran University is preparing to come together this week to remember two student-athletes killed in a crash in Seguin , as the university's Bulldog community mourns their loss. The university announced a memorial service for A'Jean (AJ) Augustine, 20, of Houston, and Deyreck Dean, 23, of Rockwall, scheduled for 11 a.m. Thursday, November 5, in Jackson Auditorium. "The Bulldog Family is devastated by the loss of two of our own this week," the university said in its announcement. The gathering will give students, faculty, staff, teammates and loved ones an opportunity to celebrate the lives of Augustine and Dean, grieve their absence and pray for their families, according to the university. A short reception will follow the service. Those unable to attend in person can watch the service through a university livestream. Augustine and Dean were killed early Monday, November 2, in a single-vehicle crash on State Highway 46 in Seguin, according to police. The crash was reported at approximately 2:38 a.m. in the 1900 block of State Highway 46 North. A 2012 Kia Sorento was traveling southbound at a high rate of speed when the driver lost control, crossed into the northbound lanes and struck a guardrail, according to a preliminary police report. Both occupants were pronounced dead at the scene. In an earlier statement to MySA, Texas Lutheran described Augustine and Dean as beloved members of the university community whose loss would be felt across campus. Both students were connected to the university's football program. Augustine was an active member of the 2026 team, listed as a junior kicker on the Bulldogs' roster. Dean previously played for the team as a senior linebacker, with his athletic eligibility expiring after the 2025 season. The livestream can be found here. Sign up for Afternoon Headlines, MySA's free newsletter bringing you San Antonio's top stories of the day. This article originally published at Details emerge following crash that killed 2 Texas Lutheran football players .

The FOX Sports analyst believes the Dolphins could make the biggest move of the next offseason by acquiring Baltimore’s two-time MVP. With Jackson facing another extended absence and his contract approaching a decision point, Wright sees Miami as a destination that could appeal to both the quarterback and a franchise searching for answers. Nick Wright Predicts Lamar Jackson Will Become Dolphins’ Starter Appearing on “The Herd,” Wright made a direct prediction about where Jackson will play next season. “I think Lamar Jackson is the Week 1 starting quarterback next year for the Miami Dolphins,” Wright said in the clip shared by the show . He built his case around Miami potentially holding a valuable draft pick, its financial direction and Jackson’s connection to Florida. “I think the Dolphins are going to have a top-three pick. The Dolphins cleaned up their cap,” Wright said. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor “I think he would accept a trade to Miami because of the Florida roots. I think that might be where this is headed.” Miami fell to 1-6 after Sunday’s 24-19 loss to New England. That record makes a high selection plausible, although the final draft order remains months away. Wright’s proposal would give the Dolphins an established quarterback with a résumé few potential acquisitions could match. That record makes a high selection plausible, although the final draft order remains months away. Wright’s proposal would give the Dolphins an established quarterback with a résumé few potential acquisitions could match. Wright was predicting a possible outcome, and the supplied clip contained no announcement of trade discussions or a request from Jackson. Jackson’s deal includes a no-trade clause, giving his willingness to approve a destination practical significance. His contract runs through 2027, so a move next offseason would require a transaction while he remains under contract. Jackson’s Latest Injury Raises Difficult Questions for Baltimore The discussion followed Jackson’s thumb injury on Baltimore’s opening offensive snap against Buffalo. item.title: Yamal And Raphinha Get 8.5 | Barcelona Players Rated In Impressive Win Vs Aston Villa
item.description: Yamal And Raphinha Get 8.5 | Barcelona Players Rated In Impressive Win Vs Aston Villa Barcelona entertained Aston Villa at the Nou Camp earlier tonight as they hoped to secure a win at home in the UEFA Champions League. The Catalan giants made a quick start to the game and got their noses ahead in the seventh minute thanks to Lamine Yamal’s goal. Hansi Flick’s men went into the half-time break 1-0 up on the scoreline. Raphinha doubled Barca’s advantage in the 52nd minute before going on to score again in the 64th minute. The match ended with the Catalan giants securing an impressive 3-0 win at the Nou Camp. Let’s take a look at how each Barcelona player fared during the clash against the Villans. GK: Joan Garcia – 7/10 Garcia made one solid save at the back and did well to secure a clean sheet tonight. RB: Brian Farinas – 7/10 He came back to defend when needed and was tidy with his ball distribution. CB: Pau Cubarsi – 7/10 Cubarsi gave a good account of himself on the defensive end of the field and was a strong presence in the air. CB: Gerard Martin – 7.5/10 He cleared his lines when he could and was good on the ball. BARCELONA, SPAIN – NOVEMBER 03: Raphinha of FC Barcelona celebrates scoring his team’s second goal with teammate Lamine Yamal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between FC Barcelona and Aston Villa FC at Camp Nou on November 03, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) LB: Joao Cancelo – 8/10 He was a positive influence at both ends of the field and has an assist to show for his efforts. CM: Pedri – 7/10 Pedri anchored the midfield well and made two good chances going forward. CM: Rodri – 6.5/10 He anchored the midfield relatively well but offered very little in the final third. CM: Fermin Lopez – 8/10 Lopez was a constant menace inside the opponent’s half and has an assist to his name. RW: Lamine Yamal – 8.5/10 He made a few dangerous runs with the ball and managed to score the opener in the seventh minute ST: Raphinha – 8.5/10 Raphinha scored a quick-fire brace in the second half to help Barcelona secure a convincing win tonight. LW: Anthony Gordon – 7.5/10 He caught the eye at times, but there was no goal for him. CM: Marc Bernal – 6.5/10 He offered decent protection for his teammates at the back. ST: Gabriel Jesus – 7/10 Jesus was lively after coming off the bench. CM: Frenkie de Jong – 6/10 He offered very little after coming on in the 69th minute. Gavi made one good chance in the final third.

item.title: NASCAR VP explains Carson Hocevar, Josh Berry penalties
item.description: Motorsport photo NASCAR Vice President of Competition Elton Sawyer took to SiriusXM Radio on Tuesday to explain the rationale behind a pair of penalties to Carson Hocevar and Josh Berry for brake checking over the weekend at Martinsville Speedway. First and foremost, the decision to issue the $100,000 fine to Hocevar and the $50,000 fine to Berry, plus 25 driver points each, came down to SMT data. NASCAR could see very decisively that both drivers retaliated on Sunday by slamming on their brakes and literally destroying the cars behind them. In the case of Hocevar, the Spire No. 77 hard braked directly in front of Austin Cindric four times on the straightaways, even with spotter Tyler Green saying repeatedly ‘Carson stop,’ without a commensurate response. Spire Motorsports took independent action from NASCAR earlier in the day by suspending Hocevar for the season finale this weekend at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Berry hard braked once on corner exit ahead of Ryan Blaney , which also forced the victim to go behind the wall, and Sawyer told Sirius Speedway host Dave Moody that this would not be tolerated. Read Also: NASCAR issues penalties to Carson Hocevar and Josh Berry for Martinsville brake-checks Spire Motorsports suspends Carson Hocevar, parking him for NASCAR finale “I think the world that we live in today with the amount of data we can pull off the cars and go back and review that, we can make better decisions,” Sawyer said. “The one thing that I would add and something that we're looking at is how we can do a better job, we as NASCAR, do a better job in officiating this within the race. “We would love to not be talking about this today, would love to be talking about going to Homestead-Miami to crown three very deserving champions, whoever they may be, Friday night, Saturday or Sunday, but unfortunately, we're talking about this today. But what we really strive is to get it right. And sometimes you have to wait just a little bit to get all the data and get all the information to be able to do that.” With that said, Sawyer does aim for NASCAR to move towards being more capable of making just calls in real time. item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo NASCAR Vice President of Competition Elton Sawyer took to SiriusXM Radio on Tuesday to explain the rationale behind a pair of penalties to Carson Hocevar and Josh Berry for brake checking over the weekend at Martinsville Speedway. First and foremost, the decision to issue the $100,000 fine to Hocevar and the $50,000 fine to Berry, plus 25 driver points each, came down to SMT data. NASCAR could see very decisively that both drivers retaliated on Sunday by slamming on their brakes and literally destroying the cars behind them. In the case of Hocevar, the Spire No. 77 hard braked directly in front of Austin Cindric four times on the straightaways, even with spotter Tyler Green saying repeatedly ‘Carson stop,’ without a commensurate response. Spire Motorsports took independent action from NASCAR earlier in the day by suspending Hocevar for the season finale this weekend at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Berry hard braked once on corner exit ahead of Ryan Blaney , which also forced the victim to go behind the wall, and Sawyer told Sirius Speedway host Dave Moody that this would not be tolerated. Read Also: NASCAR issues penalties to Carson Hocevar and Josh Berry for Martinsville brake-checks Spire Motorsports suspends Carson Hocevar, parking him for NASCAR finale “I think the world that we live in today with the amount of data we can pull off the cars and go back and review that, we can make better decisions,” Sawyer said. “The one thing that I would add and something that we're looking at is how we can do a better job, we as NASCAR, do a better job in officiating this within the race. “We would love to not be talking about this today, would love to be talking about going to Homestead-Miami to crown three very deserving champions, whoever they may be, Friday night, Saturday or Sunday, but unfortunately, we're talking about this today. But what we really strive is to get it right. And sometimes you have to wait just a little bit to get all the data and get all the information to be able to do that.” With that said, Sawyer does aim for NASCAR to move towards being more capable of making just calls in real time. Sawyer explained that NASCAR took this very seriously because it was the drivers that came to the Sanctioning Body and asked for softer bumpers in the first place. Some wanted softer bumpers to lessen the impact felt by drivers in the cars. Others wanted softer front bumpers to prevent drivers from divebombing each other in lieu of cleaner passes. So that Hocevar and Berry weaponized that on Sunday required a response. “We knew Martinsville would be the first test as far as being able to, how they could bump and run, and that's part of our DNA, that's part of Martinsville,” Sawyer said. “But what rose to a level of real concern for us was that they had taken the structure of the front of the car and used that as an antic or a strategy to basically ruin other drivers' days and then we felt like we had to step in.” Hocevar was fined $100,000 compared to the $50,000 for Berry because Sawyer said NASCAR has had numerous 'behavioral meetings' with the young driver over the past several years. "We just felt like after reviewing all the data and the audio, that this one rose to a level that it needed to be more than just the 50,000 that Josh got," Sawyer said. Sawyer also said that Spire's decision to suspend Hocevar had no bearing on what NASCAR chose to do. That was an entirely independent choice. The obvious question after all of this is if NASCAR went too far in softening the front bumpers and if the league needs to reverse course. Sawyer said no, but hedged the answer with a maybe at the same time. “We know a lot more today than we knew yesterday, and we'll know a lot more tomorrow about this situation as far as the car and how we want to react going forward with it,” Sawyer said. “But we're always learning, as we've said many, many times. And this is a safety initiative that our sport has had for decades and it's not a destination, it's a journey. “We'll continue to look at the cars and what we can do to make them as safe as possible. We know that motorsports in general is inherently a dangerous sport and we want to do everything we can to make our competitors and our fans as safe as possible. “So to get to the actual point there, we will go back and look at this and see what adjustments we can make to the car that will also give us some of the best racing, short track racing that our fans deserve and that is a little bumping and moving cars and the tire marks – things we have accustomed to loving about our short tracks. So yes, we will address that as well.” To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: The polls are open! Vote for the top Tulare County athlete of the week
item.description: Visalia Times-Delta/Tulare Advance-Register readers can now vote for their favorite high school athletes. The poll closes at noon Friday, Nov. 6. There are no restrictions, so vote now and vote often. Please do not email your votes. Here are the choices for this week: Adan Aldana, football, Woodlake: Aldana rumbled for 122 yards rushing and a touchdown to lift the Tigers to an outright East Sequoia League championship. Connor Cain, football, Golden West: Cain scored 4 total touchdowns (3 receiving, 1 rushing) and finished with 8 catches for 89 yards as the Trailblazers won their fourth straight Battle for the Saddle rivalry game. Leonardo Coronado, football, Orosi: Coronado rushed for 128 yards and 3 touchdowns as the Cardinals captured an outright East Sequoia League-Redwood championship. Emma Crisp, girls flag football, Redwood: Crisp passed for 326 yards and 4 touchdowns in a shutout playoff win over Lompoc. Mike Ennis, football, Porterville: Ennis was nearly perfect in the Granite Bowl victory, completing 18-of-20 passes for 231 yards and 3 touchdowns. He also ran for 101 yards and scored 3 rushing touchdowns. J.J. Guereca, football, Lindsay: Guereca caught 3 passes for 125 yards and 2 touchdowns as the Cardinals won the Bell Game. Nash McElree, football, Redwood: McElree completed 82% of his throws, hitting 19-of-23 passes for 251 yards and 2 touchdowns to lead the Rangers to a win in the annual Cowhide rivalry game. Landan Seechan, football, Tulare Western: Seechan scored a receiving touchdown to help the Mustangs win the Bell Game for the first time since 2019. VOTE HERE More: Tulare Western clinches outright EYL title with Bell Game win More: See the first-round matchups for Tulare County football teams How to nominate an Athlete of the Week Nominations are based on information available to the Times-Delta. All high school varsity players from Tulare County can be on the ballot. Nominations must be received by Monday morning following that week's games for consideration. Anyone can nominate an athlete of the week for every sport. Nominate next week’s ballot through email. Readers can email nominations to sports reporter Vongni Yang at vyang2@visaliatimesdelta.com. Please include a player’s statistics and a photo if possible. This article originally appeared on Visalia Times-Delta: The polls are open! Vote for the top Tulare County athlete of the week

item.title: ‘A lot of lies’ – Bruno Fernandes says Michael Carrick was ‘right’ to drop him against Bournemouth and denies rift
item.description: ‘A lot of lies’ – Bruno Fernandes says Michael Carrick was ‘right’ to drop him against Bournemouth and denies rift Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes insists there are no issues between him and boss Michael Carrick – and hopes his side’s win over Roma can be the start of a turnaround this season. The 3-2 victory provided a much-needed boost for United following a run of nine games without a win. Fernandes was dropped to the bench for his side’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth last month following comments made after their 4-1 loss to Como, in which he questioned the team’s approach . But the United skipper played down any perceived problems between him and Carrick and says he is firmly focused on turning things around. “The club needed that win, the players needed that win,” he told Amazon Prime. “We have been working so hard to get out of this situation all together. “It’s been tough, there’s been a lot of speculation in the media. A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, that we have cleared the air after. Nothing like that happened. “The manager took the decision to put me on the bench because I wasn’t performing and that’s fair. “Everyone thought that was a punishment for the words that I had. If it was, it was right. The manager is the one who makes the decisions. I have to accept that. “It doesn’t change the belief I have in the manager and the staff and every player in this club. It doesn’t change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me.” United have faced mounting pressure following their recent struggles, with supporters growing increasingly frustrated by the team’s performances. Fernandes acknowledged those frustrations but stressed that the players were equally desperate to turn their fortunes around. “It’s been a long time that we didn’t get the win and it’s been frustrating for them as much as it has been for us too,” he said. “But we didn’t take that in the wrong way. We took it in a good way because it’s normal, because fans want to win games. “They’ve been used to seeing this club at the top winning games and winning trophies and for them it’s been so frustrating to see the club in this situation. “I want to make everyone aware that we are all frustrated with the situation at the moment and we all want to get out of this. Hopefully this win today is the start of something good for us.” Reflecting on the comeback victory over Roma, in which United came from two goals down thanks to a Fernandes penalty and Matheus Cunha double, the Portugal international urged his side to build on the win. “It’s been a tough period for us, we have not been able to perform in the way we want, to get the results we want,” he added. “We’ve done some good bits, but not had the consistency to do it through a full game to get more results and it’s been tough. “But today was important to get a win. We knew after half-time we still had the fans with us, we felt at any moment that we could change

item.title: USA Soccer’s Balogun Returns To Action For Monaco
item.description: Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - United States Training - University of Washington, Seattle, Washington, U.S. - July 3, 2026 Folarin Balogun of the U.S. during training IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Steven Bisig Folarin Balogun finally broke his scoring drought for Monaco. The United States men’s national team striker is back in the mix for the Conference League, according to Fox Sports . He earned his spot after Ansu Fati got hurt and had to leave the squad list. This move clears a huge path for Balogun to get more playing time. It also fixes a strange situation that kept him on the bench for weeks. The change happened right before the next round of games. Balogun’s name now appears on the official roster shown on Tuesday. He was missing from the list just a short time ago. The club decided to swap him in because Fati cannot play. The French daily L’Equipe reported that Fati is out for two months. He suffered the injury in a match against Lille on Oct. 25. That gap left Monaco needing a forward, and Balogun stepped up. A Rough Path to the Field Getting to this point was not easy for the American striker. He only played as a substitute this season. He has featured in five games total. A 3-1 defeat at Paris FC on Sunday marked his first goal of the season. That goal matters more now because it ends a dry spell. It also proves he can score even when the team struggles. The road to this moment was blocked by transfer drama. Balogun was close to joining Everton in late August. A deal for a reported £40 million (with add-ons) was on the table. He pulled out of the move at the last minute . Doubts from the English club regarding his health made him uneasy. He did not want to sign with a team that questioned his medical results. This decision kept him at Monaco, but it caused confusion. World Cup Drama and New Chances The striker faced other hurdles before this season even started. A red card during the World Cup caused a major controversy. He got the card in a win over Bosnia and Herzegovina. The suspension was one game, but it was deferred by FIFA. U.S. President Donald Trump intervened to help. Gianni Infantino received a call to check if the red card review was possible. The request worked. Balogun was allowed to play in the round of 16. He had a forgettable performance as the U.S. lost to Belgium. Now the focus shifts to the upcoming matches. The Conference League saw Monaco secure victories in its opening two matches. They beat CSKA Sofia and Freiburg. The team has tough matches coming up. They will play FC Nordsjælland on Thursday. They also face Hearts, Brighton, and Lincoln Red Imps later. Balogun needs to keep scoring if he wants to stay in the starting lineup. The clock is ticking for him to prove he is ready. The squad list is set, and he is now one of the forwards. Fans will watch closely to see if he can lead the attack.

item.title: Man Utd snap winless streak with Roma comeback
item.description: Matheus Cunha scored twice in Manchester United's comeback against Roma (Oli SCARFF) Manchester United roared back from 2-0 down to give beleaguered manager Michael Carrick a lifeline with a memorable 3-2 win over Roma at Old Trafford. The unrest among the home fans bordered on mutiny after Roma surged into a 2-0 lead inside 20 minutes through Matias Soule and Donyell Malen. But United ended a nine-game winless run in all competitions thanks to Matheus Cunha's double after a twice-taken Bruno Fernandes penalty had reduced the deficit. "This place does incredible things, does magical things," said Carrick. "I spoke with them at half-time a little bit about how this place can change and it only takes one moment. It certainly did that and the boys made every little bit of every little opportunity. Fantastic in the end." The decision to hand Carrick a stay of execution looked to have backfired in a lifeless first half United performance. Roma, though, failed to slay their ghosts of four previous defeats at Old Trafford in another spectacular Champions League collapse. Gian Piero Gasperini's men lost 4-3 to Real Madrid last month after leading 3-1 with just eight minutes remaining. "A game lasts 90 minutes," said Gasperini. "They stepped it up in the second half but we could have done more to safeguard the score." - Cunha's costly celebration - Carrick reacted to Lisandro Martinez's foolish red card in a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday by dropping the Argentine international. It made little difference as his disorganised defence was torn apart inside the opening 20 minutes. Soule was afforded acres of space to control Rodrigo Mora's pass and slot past Senne Lammens on 11 minutes. Moments later United were left completely exposed again down their left and Malen converted a penalty after Soule's shot hit the outstretched hand of Ayden Heaven. The game was temporarily stopped midway through the first half by supporters throwing tennis balls onto the field, accompanied by chants calling for with United's unpopular owners, the American-based Glazer family, to sell the club. United were dealt a further blow inside two minutes of the second half when £70 million ($94 million) signing Carlos Baleba pulled up with a suspected severe hamstring injury after bursting into the Roma box. Yet, Carrick's luck turned just before the hour mark when Cunha won a generous penalty award for minimal contact by Gianluca Mancini. Fernandes's first spot-kick was saved by Roma's third-choice goalkeeper Devis Vasquez, but was given a reprieve by encroaching by the visitors. The United captain smashed home at the second attempt to kickstart the comeback. Seconds later Bryan Mbeumo hit the inside of both posts after being played in by Cunha. United were gifted the equaliser seven minutes from time when Leonardo Balerdi's swipe at fresh air gave Cunha the simplest task to tap in. "This place does incredible things, does magical things," said Carrick. "I spoke with them at half-time a little bit about how this place can change and it only takes one moment. The decision to hand Carrick a stay of execution looked to have backfired in a lifeless first half United performance. Roma, though, failed to slay their ghosts of four previous defeats at Old Trafford in another spectacular Champions League collapse. Gian Piero Gasperini's men lost 4-3 to Real Madrid last month after leading 3-1 with just eight minutes remaining. "A game lasts 90 minutes," said Gasperini. "They stepped it up in the second half but we could have done more to safeguard the score." - Cunha's costly celebration - Carrick reacted to Lisandro Martinez's foolish red card in a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday by dropping the Argentine international. It made little difference as his disorganised defence was torn apart inside the opening 20 minutes. Soule was afforded acres of space to control Rodrigo Mora's pass and slot past Senne Lammens on 11 minutes. Moments later United were left completely exposed again down their left and Malen converted a penalty after Soule's shot hit the outstretched hand of Ayden Heaven. The game was temporarily stopped midway through the first half by supporters throwing tennis balls onto the field, accompanied by chants calling for with United's unpopular owners, the American-based Glazer family, to sell the club. United were dealt a further blow inside two minutes of the second half when £70 million ($94 million) signing Carlos Baleba pulled up with a suspected severe hamstring injury after bursting into the Roma box. Yet, Carrick's luck turned just before the hour mark when Cunha won a generous penalty award for minimal contact by Gianluca Mancini. Fernandes's first spot-kick was saved by Roma's third-choice goalkeeper Devis Vasquez, but was given a reprieve by encroaching by the visitors. The United captain smashed home at the second attempt to kickstart the comeback. Seconds later Bryan Mbeumo hit the inside of both posts after being played in by Cunha. United were gifted the equaliser seven minutes from time when Leonardo Balerdi's swipe at fresh air gave Cunha the simplest task to tap in. Three minutes later, the Brazilian thundered a shot past Vasquez at his near post and flung himself into the crowd in what proved to be a costly celebration. Cunha was booked and then shown a second yellow card moments later for a wild lunge in stoppage time. But the 10 men held on to breathe new life into United's Champions League campaign after back-to-back defeats against Atletico Madrid and Como. Whether it proves to be a turning point or just another temporary reprieve for Carrick remains to be seen. "It's one game, so it depends on what happens next and we've got to capitalise on that," added Carrick. "To see the supporters going home happy, it's what we live for. To give them performances and nights like this." kca/lp

item.title: Colton Herta to run Cadillac FP1 in Brazil as FIA superlicense quest continues
item.description: Motorsport photo Cadillac test driver Colton Herta will conduct his sixth Friday practice session of the F1 season at this weekend's Sao Paulo GP to collect his missing FIA superlicense point required to race in the series. Herta, who has been building up for an F1 campaign with private testing, FP1 sessions and a troubled F2 campaign, needs 40 points to obtain the required FIA superlicense. Cadillac believed the former IndyCar ace had reached that threshold last week in Mexico, but it soon emerged the Californian was still one point shy amid confusion over his previous IndyCar results. Cadillac will now rectify that error by handing Herta another Friday FP1 session in Sergio Perez's car, which yields a single point. Teams are only required to run a rookie in four FP1 sessions per year, but Sao Paulo will be Herta's sixth of the season as the squad is keen for Herta to finally obtain the license. That allows the team to keep its options open as it considers retaining incumbent Valtteri Bottas for a second year alongside Perez, or handing Herta his F1 debut in 2027. "I’m really looking forward to getting back behind the wheel of the MAC-26 for another FP1 session," Herta said. "Interlagos is such an iconic, historic track, and driving an F1 car around there is going to be an awesome experience. "Every time I’ve stepped into the car this year, from Barcelona to Budapest, COTA and Mexico City, I’ve felt more comfortable and better integrated with the engineering team. My goal for Friday morning in Brazil is the same: execute the run plan cleanly, give Checo and the engineers the best possible setup data to start their weekend, and keep building on my progress in the car. I’m grateful to the team for giving me this opportunity." Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing crash Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing crash Cadillac heads to Brazil after a bruising Mexico weekend, which ended with Bottas suffering a high-speed crash in the race due to a sudden front-left suspension failure. Team principal Marcin Budkowski said the team had "implemented mitigations" to avoid a repeat. "Following our post-race investigations, Valtteri suffered a suspension failure, and we have implemented mitigations going forward," Budkowski said. "I’m also pleased to see Colton return to the MAC-26 for another FP1 outing, stepping in for Checo. His growth in the car across his sessions has been impressive, and his feedback remains invaluable to our 2027 development program." Herta's bid to obtain his superlicense hit a snag when his car broke down in Monza, leaving the 26-year-old short of the 100km threshold required for the session to award a point. In Brazil, 24 laps of the Interlagos circuit will satisfy that requirement. "Every time I’ve stepped into the car this year, from Barcelona to Budapest, COTA and Mexico City, I’ve felt more comfortable and better integrated with the engineering team. My goal for Friday morning in Brazil is the same: execute the run plan cleanly, give Checo and the engineers the best possible setup data to start their weekend, and keep building on my progress in the car. I’m grateful to the team for giving me this opportunity." Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing crash Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing crash Cadillac heads to Brazil after a bruising Mexico weekend, which ended with Bottas suffering a high-speed crash in the race due to a sudden front-left suspension failure. Team principal Marcin Budkowski said the team had "implemented mitigations" to avoid a repeat. "Following our post-race investigations, Valtteri suffered a suspension failure, and we have implemented mitigations going forward," Budkowski said. "I’m also pleased to see Colton return to the MAC-26 for another FP1 outing, stepping in for Checo. His growth in the car across his sessions has been impressive, and his feedback remains invaluable to our 2027 development program." Herta's bid to obtain his superlicense hit a snag when his car broke down in Monza, leaving the 26-year-old short of the 100km threshold required for the session to award a point. In Brazil, 24 laps of the Interlagos circuit will satisfy that requirement. (Photo by Eakin Howard/Getty Images) Getty The Golden State Warriors lack frontcourt depth, and the absence of Kristaps Porzingis to begin the year has been a big hit for the team hoping to stay competitive in the final seasons left in the Stephen Curry era. The Warriors are reportedly exploring a Porzingis trade, and with that, a few replacement options have emerged as names the team could go after to capitalize on the time left they have with Curry. With that, one big man in particular who remains a top Warriors trade target is Domantas Sabonis of the Sacramento Kings, and in a new proposal, Golden State takes a big risk to add the center, who is not happy playing for his current team, to land a solid Porzingis replacement. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) Writing for Bleacher Report amid Golden State’s need to upgrade the frontcourt and add a Porzingis replacement, Andy Bailey offered up a Warriors trade proposal that sees the team add Sabonis from the Kings. Here’s his trade idea: Golden State Warriors Receive: Domantas Sabonis Sacramento Kings Receive: Draymond Green (trade-eligible on December 15), Kristaps Porziņģis, Will Richard and a top-four protected 2032 first-round pick “The Golden State Warriors’ better-than-expected start makes a Draymond Green trade harder to imagine, but they look like a near-ideal landing spot for Sabonis, and they simply can’t get him without including Green or Jimmy Butler,” he wrote. “The more logical approach, assuming the Warriors really want to chase one more title with Stephen Curry, is to pair Green’s salary with the Kristaps Porziņģis contract, which was essentially designed to be a human trade exception.” Moving Green might be difficult for the Warriors, but as seen with his recent ejection , there’s clearly still some major holes i

(Photo by Kelley L Cox/Getty Images) Getty Domantas Sabonis wants to leave Kings Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - MARCH 27: Kristaps Porzingis #7 of the Golden State Warriors celebrates with Will Richard #3 after a three-point basket against the Washington Wizards in the first quarter at Chase Center on March 27, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Eakin Howard/Getty Images) Getty The Golden State Warriors lack frontcourt depth, and the absence of Kristaps Porzingis to begin the year has been a big hit for the team hoping to stay competitive in the final seasons left in the Stephen Curry era. The Warriors are reportedly exploring a Porzingis trade, and with that, a few replacement options have emerged as names the team could go after to capitalize on the time left they have with Curry. With that, one big man in particular who remains a top Warriors trade target is Domantas Sabonis of the Sacramento Kings, and in a new proposal, Golden State takes a big risk to add the center, who is not happy playing for his current team, to land a solid Porzingis replacement. Warriors Domantas Sabonis Trade Idea Getty INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA – OCTOBER 21: Domantas Sabonis #11 of the Sacramento Kings looks on against the Los Angeles Clippers at Intuit Dome on October 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) Writing for Bleacher Report amid Golden State’s need to upgrade the frontcourt and add a Porzingis replacement, Andy Bailey offered up a Warriors trade proposal that sees the team add Sabonis from the Kings. Here’s his trade idea: Golden State Warriors Receive: Domantas Sabonis Sacramento Kings Receive: Draymond Green (trade-eligible on December 15), Kristaps Porziņģis, Will Richard and a top-four protected 2032 first-round pick “The Golden State Warriors’ better-than-expected start makes a Draymond Green trade harder to imagine, but they look like a near-ideal landing spot for Sabonis, and they simply can’t get him without including Green or Jimmy Butler,” he wrote. “The more logical approach, assuming the Warriors really want to chase one more title with Stephen Curry, is to pair Green’s salary with the Kristaps Porziņģis contract, which was essentially designed to be a human trade exception.” Moving Green might be difficult for the Warriors, but as seen with his recent ejection , there’s clearly still some major holes in his game, as he isn’t the same type of player he was during the team’s dynasty run a decade ago. Sabonis is also reportedly frustrated in Sacramento right now, and if he is available in a trade for a team like Golden State, he could be a huge upgrade, especially with Porzingis still out. Domantas Sabonis is unhappy and wants out of Sacramento, per @BannedMacMahon “Quite frankly, Sabonis wants out of there, and if they can move him, they would. So he's not happy.” pic.twitter.com/YqLwiU5jAf — NBABase (@TheNBABase) November 2, 2026 “Sabonis would be a dramatic upgrade over Green in scoring and rebounding. He’s at least as good a passer (though maybe not quite as good a creator). And it’s easy to imagine the fit between him and Yaxel Lendeborg. Curry’s off-ball movement around either (or both) of those interior hubs would be nearly impossible to stop,” Bailey added. “It’s maybe a harder sell on the other side of the deal. Neither vet seems like a longterm option for Sacramento, but Green’s deal is expiring and Porziņģis’ is only guaranteed for $3 million. They represent an opportunity for flexibility, while Sabonis’ deal is guaranteed for $48.6 million next season.” A Warriors trade proposal like this one, though risky, could be the franchise’s best option to move on from Porzingis while staying competitive after going on a hot streak to begin the 2026-27 season. Why Golden State Lands A Kristaps Porzingis Replacement Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA – MARCH 27: Kristaps Porzingis #7 of the Golden State Warriors celebrates with Will Richard #3 after a three-point basket against the Washington Wizards in the first quarter at Chase Center on March 27, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Eakin Howard/Getty Images) As mentioned, the Warriors are reportedly exploring the possibility of trading Porzingis, as he remains out indefinitely with the POTS illness he picked up a few years ago, and has yet to spend pretty much any time with the team. “Golden State has started exploring trade routes for Kristaps Porzingis, who is now seriously contemplating his future in basketball as he deals with recurring symptoms from the autoimmune condition termed as POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome), sources tell ESPN,” Shams Charania wrote in a post on X. Golden State has started exploring trade routes for Kristaps Porzingis, who is now seriously contemplating his future in basketball as he deals with recurring symptoms from the autoimmune condition termed as POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome), sources tell ESPN. pic.twitter.com/w9fb2Tk4kb — Shams Charania (@ShamsCharania) October 21, 2026 “Porzingis signed a two-year, $40 million extension with the team in June, but only $3 million of the $20 million in the second season is guaranteed, essentially making it an expiring contract. The front office strategically designed the extension without a raise between the two seasons, keeping him immediately trade-eligible instead of needing to wait until mid-December,” ESPN’s Anthony Slater wrote in subsequent reporting. With that, Sabonis becomes a very realistic replacement option. He isn’t the same caliber player he was a few seasons ago, but remains an offensive hub who could help the Warriors stay competitive over the next few seasons. The center’s scoring numbers are down, but he is averaging a league-leading 14.6 rebounds , along with 6.9 assists, while shooting 71.2% so far this year. His trade value might be low right now, and though the Warriors would have to give up Green in a trade to match salaries, this could be the one final risk Golden State takes to give Curry another shot at leading the team to a fifth title. Just a trade idea, but perhaps one the Warriors should entertain, as Porzingis remains out, and there’s no timeline for when or if he’ll ever play in the Bay Area again. item.title: Lennart Karl steals in behind Atlético Madrid to inspire Bayern Munich win
item.description: “This stadium brings back bad memories but I hope to be able to replace them with good ones,” Harry Kane had said on Monday night, and 24 hours later this was a start. A small step, perhaps, towards coming back on 5 June and having a second go at winning the Champions League in the arena where he lost the 2019 final . On his first European outing since winning the Ballon d’Or , the England captain was unable to score but he and his Bayern Munich team defeated Atlético Madrid, fellow semi-finalists from last season. They did so in a way that suggests that their candidacy this season is serious. It may not have been sparkling but they had been superior almost from the start, dominant in physique and football. This is a team with few weaknesses, intense and impressive throughout. All Atlético could do was resist and it never truly felt like they would be able to do that for ninety minutes; ultimately, they lasted 54. That was when Lennart Karl scored the first. The superb Konrad Laimer then added the second on a night when they racked up nineteen shots. It had been heavy going for a while, and they had been made to wait, but in the end Bayern were just that bit too good. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester United produce comeback for the ages as Cunha double floors Roma
item.description: Michael Carrick enjoyed one of his finest nights as a Manchester United player in the Champions League against Roma, scoring twice in a 7-1 win in the quarter-final, second leg in 2007. Amid an atmosphere of continued fan anger towards the United ownership, Carrick’s team had been implausibly bad. item.title: Raphinha underlines Barcelona’s class to give Aston Villa a reality check
item.description: This was a chastening night for Aston Villa, and a familiar one for Unai Emery in this corner of town. On a processional night at the Camp Nou Barcelona produced a performance of unhurried, high-grade incision, easing to a 3-0 Champions League victory that never really seemed to tip into an actual close-quarter contest before it was already gone. “There are a lot of things to learn today,” Emery said afterwards. “Overall we are competing fantastically in the Champions League; we have nine points. Today, we saw there is still more to do to get to this level. Even sometimes in this match we were close to achieving it. We had chances, but we must be ruthless in the final third. Three-nil maybe was more than we deserved.” Continue reading...

item.title: Tenerife footballer Jesús de Miguel dies aged 30 after on-pitch collision
item.description: Police homicide division opens judicial proceedings He was struck in the chest when challenging for ball Spanish football was in shock on Tuesday after the Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel died after a collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during a match in the second division. The homicide division of the national police has opened judicial proceedings into a possible involuntary manslaughter, a routine procedure after any death not by natural causes. The chief public prosecutor in Santa Cruz de Tenerife told the state news agency EFE that it was “very difficult” for a case to come to court. Tenerife announced that De Miguel had died at 8am on Tuesday after he had been taken into intensive care on Monday afternoon. He did not regain consciousness after a cardiorespiratory arrest. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | West Ham want promotion – so it’s time to call in an understated club legend
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While Football Daily hasn’t actually seen much of West Ham this season, we’ve noted enough of their results to presume they were doing OK in their attempt to bounce back to the Premier League after relegation. Less than a third of the way through the Championship season under Nuno Espírito Santo, they’d already spanked six without reply past both Wrexham and Lincoln, while scoring three or more in wins over Wolves, Derby and Bolton. However, it turns out that of the 13 matches they’ve played in a league that is famously difficult to get out of (unless you were Sheffield Wednesday last season ), they have actually lost three times and currently sit in eighth place, a whopping six points off leaders Middlesbrough. Given the context of such an unbridgeable chasm, it is small wonder West Ham fans woke up to news that Nuno had been unceremoniously bounced out of the London Stadium with a P45 in hand. While my heart aches for Jesús de Miguel, who has died after a collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono, I shudder to think the trauma that shall haunt Owono for the rest of his life. I do hope and pray the wider community understands and extends their support in his recuperation” – Krishna Moorthy. As an upgrade to Steve Plever’s suggestion of paper thin shirts [ Monday’s letters ]: how about Velcro shirts? If the bit comes off, it is a shirt pull and the offender has the honour of putting it back in place before being awarded a yellow card” – Mike Harold. To dive or not to dive seems to be biggest dilemma in the Premier League right now. It’s not. The problem with today’s highly paid professionals is that they simply have no panache at all when they go down. I recall watching Francis Lee pick up the ball on the halfway line at a mud soaked Maine Road in the late 1960s, he put his head down and headed for goal, he was determined, he was single minded. He was 30 yards from goal, he was in full flow. He was tackled from behind and then he really took off, he grew wings, he soared. I swear he landed in the penalty area over 10 yards away. He dragged himself to his feet and without a semblance of a smile smashed the well-deserved penalty, with a very heavy leather ball straight at the centre of the goal at over 70 mph. The goalkeeper, obviously no fool, simply dived out of the way. The press christened him “Lee Won Pen” He was my hero. That man had panache, he had style” – Myles Flynn. I am interested to read that Aston Villa considered the words of Jamie Carragher “unacceptable insults” . It would obviously help matters if they could publish examples of acceptable insults” – Rupert Jeffery. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: ‘An absolute afterthought’: the story of the Nigeria women’s team’s fall from grace
item.description: The Super Falcons won’t be at the World Cup and with the prize money going up, they risk being left even further behind It was a historic result in Casablanca – but not in a good way. Nigeria’s 2-1 defeat against South Africa in a playoff in August meant that the Super Falcons are missing out on the World Cup for the first time. It is a crushing blow for the most decorated national side in Africa across both men and women, one that has won no fewer than 10 Wafcon titles . The journalist and lecturer Dr Victor Ademola was in Morocco the day of the defeat. “It was a very difficult evening,” he says. “Some players were visibly emotional while others appeared to be processing what had just happened. I saw players crying as they got on to the team bus while some sat alone or remained on their phones, looking very sad.” Continue reading...

item.title: Fifa to share documents on World Cup sell-off plans with council members
item.description: Viewings to take place at Fifa’s headquarters in Zurich No direct response to Uefa’s questions on governance Fifa will grant its council members access to documents regarding the doomed Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme but has not responded directly to more than 50 questions from Uefa about its governance and recent scandals. In a letter sent to the Fifa Council by Mattias Grafström, the governing body’s secretary general, members were told material relating to FFE will be released for them to view in person at Fifa’s headquarters in Zurich. They will be allowed only to view the documents, of which the exact nature and scope are unclear, under strict confidentiality protocols. A deadline of 16 November has been set to apply for such visits; eyebrows may be raised in some quarters about the fact this is two days before candidates for the Fifa election next year are required to declare their hand. Continue reading...

item.title: Revisiting the Superclásico: a story of death, violence, colour and family
item.description: Attending Boca v River in the week I turned 60 made me recall a lifetime of experiences at the fixture Ever since the Observer Sport Monthly published a list of 50 sporting things you must do before you die with Watch Boca Juniors Play River Plate in Buenos Aires at No 1 in 2004, the biggest super derby in Argentina has been firmly positioned in the global imagination; its reputation for colour, passion and uncontainable emotion acquiring an almost glamorous sheen. The thump and thud of the coordinated chants, the shiny ticker-tape amid flare smoke matching the teams’ strips, the bounce of the concrete as tens of thousands jump in unison, mounted police surrounding the stadium, avalanche stoppers set alight, rockets aimed at players; blood and fire. Exciting, right? Continue reading...

item.title: Goals, guests and 6,561 scenarios: inside ESPN on the biggest NWSL Decision Day yet
item.description: The final day of the regular season gave fans Gotham’s Shield win, a farewell to a Seattle hero and a new part-whiparound, part-watchalong show to take it all in As a player, Ali Krieger went into NWSL Decision Day focused on one result. She was Gotham FC’s captain in 2023, the first time the league played all of the final games of the regular season simultaneously. The job, she remembers, was to not worry about the other games going on. Three years later, Krieger spent Decision Day with eyes on not one game but eight. For the first time, all of the final games of the NWSL season were aired by the same network. Krieger, now a lead analyst for ESPN, and host Kelsey Riggs Cuff anchored the coverage from headquarters in Bristol with a show that was part whiparound, part watchalong, and ultimately wholly new for the 14-year-old league. Continue reading...

item.title: Arsenal have everything they need to repeat as Premier League champions | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Sunday’s win at Liverpool showed the Gunners are deeper, more experienced, and are playing against a weaker class of contenders than last season Sign up for our free newsletter here Arsenal are three points clear at the top of the Premier League table . But given the team in second are Manchester City, who are likely to be facing at the very least a major points deduction , perhaps more significant is that they are five clear of Brighton in third. The season of domination that many anticipated from the champions appears to be coming to pass. Liverpool challenged them on Sunday. There was a 20-minute spell before half-time when they swarmed all over Arsenal, and Anfield felt at least like it did in the golden years of Jürgen Klopp, when it buzzed with an energy that could overwhelm visitors. But Arsenal got through that, reset at half-time, and navigated the second half with relative comfort. For the second league game running, they denied Liverpool a shot on target. This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Led by Liam Rosenior and backed by billionaires, Paris FC are now a force in Ligue 1 | Luke Entwistle
item.description: After a huge summer and with PSG’s other rivals falling away, their city rivals are aiming to ‘be one of the biggest clubs in Europe’ By Get French Football News It is hard to know what Pierre Ferracci found stranger: the fact that he was fully suited among a set of bare-chested Paris FC ultras singing his name or that, behind him, in what was the final game of his presidency, his team were playing Monaco off the park. “I didn’t see any of the first 15 minutes of the game because I was with the ultras,” he admitted. On the pitch, as well as in the stands, was evidence of how far his side has come since he joined back in 2006. At that time, Les Parisiens were in the amateur third tier of French football. Ferracci arrived initially in an administrative function before becoming owner and president in 2012. It was not until 2017 that his side reached Ligue 2. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Aston Villa, ‘unacceptable insults’ and thin-skinned clutching of pearls
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! When Jamie Carragher appeared as a pundit on Sky Sports Super Sunday, Football Daily was surprised he didn’t have a solicitor sitting alongside him, occasionally jotting notes on a pad or leaning over to give whispered instructions and answer “no comment” to any leading questions about Trey Nyoni starting ahead of Ryan Gravenberch. On Friday night, the former Liverpool defender was subjected to a threat of legal action from Aston Villa, who took such grave exception to some “unacceptable insults” he had rained down on them from his podcast pulpit, that they were ready to call in the heavy legal artillery and stop him from preventing their “ascension in English and European football”. Taking a leaf out of the tried-and-much-ridiculed Nottingham Forest playbook , Villa chair Nassef Sawiris appears to have eschewed contacting Carragher through the usual formal channels and instead cajoled some unfortunate junior comms staffer to make the portentous announcement on their Social Media Disgraces. Continue reading...

item.title: From VHS dreams to San Siro glory: Amorim’s Milan surge puts rivals on notice | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Inspired by the legendary Milan sides of his youth, the manager gave his side a lift with a tactical victory over Inter Ruben Amorim had waited a lifetime for his first Milan derby. As a kid growing up in Lisbon, he supported two football teams. There was the local one, Benfica, whose games he attended so early in life that his father has recalled changing nappies in the stands of the old Estádio da Luz. And the other one that captivated him from overseas. “I remember watching tapes of that Milan team with [Paolo] Maldini, [Franco] Baresi, [Ruud] Gullit, [Frank] Rijkaard, [Dejan] Savicevic,” Amorim told the Portuguese newspaper Expresso in 2017. “My childhood dreams were to play for Benfica and Milan. I’ve fulfilled one. Now I suppose I’ll have to become a coach for the other!” Continue reading...

item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Kang could have a problem and how long can Slegers hang on?
item.description: Arsenal dropped points again despite dominating while Lauren James had to go off in Chelsea’s 6-0 win at Charlton London City Lionesses may have lost 2-1 to champions Manchester City, but their performances and league position have shown their European aspirations are far from unrealistic. Aided by Arsenal’s poor start, London City are third in the WSL table and were frustrated to end the day with a six-point gap to the top two after dominating in Bromley. “It’s doubly frustrating, because I think the result was not the one we deserve,” said their coach, Eder Maestre. “Manchester City are more mature. They are more used to it. When you have this consistency and you are very used to playing these kinds of games, maybe you have more experience.” Maestre’s team have a three-point lead over fourth-placed Tottenham and if they continue their upwards trajectory and qualify for the Champions League, Uefa will be forced to tackle the possible scenario of two Michele Kang-owned clubs, London City and OL Lyonnes, qualifying sooner than they perhaps anticipated. item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. And then it happened: never mind that Athletic still had a derby to win and a corner to defend, forget the fact that the lead was a single goal, the visitors relentless now and 25 minutes still to resist; at the stadium everyone calls the Cathedral , a place of ritual and liturgy like no other, the entire congregation, 50,092 people, started clapping. Started and did not stop. For a minute, maybe more, it was like the match that matters most didn’t matter at all, momentarily fading until it was just him and them together. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Marco Rose’s tactics are lifting Bournemouth, Roméo Lavia makes progress with Chelsea and Roberto De Zerbi gives youth a chance at Spurs Good defending is the mark of champions. At Anfield, where Arsenal had not won in the past 13 visits, Mikel Arteta followed the orthodoxy of locking down once his team took the lead. This time around, it proved successful. Arsenal did not allow the occasion or the stadium to get to them as they have on previous occasions. In April 2023, Granit Xhaka entangling with Trent Alexander-Arnold energised home fans previously despondent that Arsenal were 2-0 up. It finished 2-2. On Sunday, Liverpool zipped around zestfully, as Andoni Iraola requests, though the final-ball quality was lacking. That owed a great deal to the organisation of the Arsenal defence. Ahead of the last international break, Brighton set a blueprint for getting the better of Arsenal in winning 3-0 . Liverpool’s squad profile might have made a similar strategy possible though Iraola’s outfit is struggling to create chances in the same volume as Brighton or his Bournemouth team. item.description: Unusually, all clubs in the top flight have the same manager with whom they began the season – but the first sacking may not be far away No Premier League manager has yet lost his job this season. In only three of the past 10 campaigns was November reached without a club making a managerial change. The 2026-27 season commencing with 11 managers who were appointed at some point in 2026 has probably contributed to the early season stability. They have to be given a chance to fashion their side as they see fit. But with roughly a quarter of the season played and only one more round of fixtures before an international break, the first sacking may not be far away. Continue reading...

item.title: A phone-free Yellow Wall: are Dortmund urging fans to be present or policing them?
item.description: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma By all appearances, things on the Yellow Wall seemed as they always had been. The stadium announcer hollered out the first names of Borussia Dortmund’s starting lineup and the supporters responded with their last names, tens of thousands of voices bellowing as one. Dozens of black and yellow flags waved over Europe’s largest standing terrace, a mass of faces fixed on the field beneath them. And then Signal Iduna Park, sold out with 81,365 fans, roared when Max Beier’s lone goal led Dortmund to victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, putting the home side even on points with Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga standings. Continue reading...

item.title: Rodman rule has been revised but the fight to keep stars in the NWSL goes on | Moving the Goalposts
item.description: Gone are the eight criteria to be a High Impact Player so clubs can spend their money on whomever they want – and the solution makes sense When Washington plays Chicago this Sunday in DC, “Rowdy Audi” will probably be full. It will also be full when the post-season starts, should they lock up their top-four position with a positive result on Decision Day. Equipped with an accessible stadium in a big city, a proud fanbase and a formidable roster rife with players qualifying for the High Impact Player (HIP) rule’s initial criteria (including Trinity Rodman, who gave the rule its moniker), the Spirit hold sway in the attendance charts. But starting next season, everyone on the Spirit will qualify for the “Rodman Rule” . So will every player in NWSL. Announced Friday, NWSL settled a grievance with the league’s Players Association, who argued that the initial criteria violated federal labor law. Continue reading...

item.description: Plus: the longest home droughts, pre-Christmas goal centuries and the first official club websites Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Justin Seven-Seven came on in the 75th minute and then scored in the 77th minute for West Brom Under-21s against Sutton United in the National League Cup. You have probably already guessed my question, but has anyone else ever scored in the same minute as their name?” wonders Peter Skilton. Readers of a certain age may recall Didier Six , the mercurial French winger who had a brief spell at Aston Villa in 1984-85. A number of you mentioned some or all of the following sixth-minute goals, which includes two in consecutive seasons against Bordeaux: Valenciennes 2-1 Nancy (agg: 2-3) Coupe de France quarter-final, 1975-76 Valenciennes 3-2 Bordeaux Ligue 1, 1976-77 Lens 2-0 Bordeaux Ligue 1, 1977-78 VfB Stuttgart 5-1 Karlsruher Bundesliga, 1981-82 Bundesliga 71 goals in 18 games Champions League 18 goals in 6 games DFB-Pokal 10 goals in 3 games Franz Beckenbauer Supercup 2 goals in 1 game Continue reading...

item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.description: Video appears to show Mao Zedong called a ‘dictator’ Dongpeng and Mengniu end deals with the player Kylian Mbappé has apologised after the Real Madrid forward was dropped by major Chinese brands for apparently joking about Mao Zedong in a video that has gone viral. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with the state-run Chinese digital newspaper The Paper reporting that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappé saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photoshopped on to that of “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappé superimposed on an image of Mao. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...
